The **Nigeria national cricket team** is the men's team that represents the country of [Nigeria](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nigeria "Nigeria") in [international cricket](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/International_cricket "International cricket"). [Cricket](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cricket "Cricket") has been played in Nigeria since the late 19th century, and the national team played their first match in 1904, when a team representing the [Lagos Colony](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lagos_Colony "Lagos Colony") played the [Gold Coast Colony](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gold_Coast_Colony "Gold Coast Colony").[[6]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nigeria_national_cricket_team#cite_note-EWC-7) The [Nigeria Cricket Association, formed in 1932](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nigeria_Cricket_Association "Nigeria Cricket Association")[[7]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nigeria_national_cricket_team#cite_note-:0-8) and at first was composed only of expats.[[8]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nigeria_national_cricket_team#cite_note-:1-9) One year later. in 1933, an organization of indigenous players was formed.[[8]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nigeria_national_cricket_team#cite_note-:1-9) Nigeria has been an associate member of the [International Cricket Council](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/International_Cricket_Council "International Cricket Council") (ICC) since 2002.[[9]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nigeria_national_cricket_team#cite_note-CAP-10)

## History

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Nigeria_national_cricket_team&action=edit&section=1 "Edit section: History")]

### Early years

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Nigeria_national_cricket_team&action=edit&section=2 "Edit section: Early years")]

Cricket has been played in Nigeria since the late 19th century when the game was introduced by the British.[[8]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nigeria_national_cricket_team#cite_note-:1-9) English missionaries and army personnel further spread the sport.[[7]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nigeria_national_cricket_team#cite_note-:0-8)Contacts between the administration in Lagos and their counterparts in [Gold Coast](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gold_Coast_(British_colony) "Gold Coast (British colony)") (now [Ghana](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ghana "Ghana")) led to an international at Race Course (now [Tafawa Balewa Square](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tafawa_Balewa_Square "Tafawa Balewa Square")), [Lagos](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lagos "Lagos") on 25 May 1904,[[10]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nigeria_national_cricket_team#cite_note-11)[[11]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nigeria_national_cricket_team#cite_note-12) the [Gold Coast](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ghana_national_cricket_team "Ghana national cricket team") winning by 22 runs.[[6]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nigeria_national_cricket_team#cite_note-EWC-7)

The match became an annual fixture and for the first three matches was multi-racial. The fourth fixture in December 1906 was for Europeans only, and the African population started their own annual fixture in 1907. Internationals stopped for the [First World War](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/First_World_War "First World War"), and did not restart until the mid-1920s.[[6]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nigeria_national_cricket_team#cite_note-EWC-7)

Between the two world wars, cricket began to become more formally organised in the country with two cricket associations for the Europeans and Africans being formed in 1932 and 1933 respectively. [First-class cricketers](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/First-class_cricket "First-class cricket") from England began to appear in the annual matches against Gold Coast,[[6]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nigeria_national_cricket_team#cite_note-EWC-7) and the 1939 match, the last before World War II, ended in a 58-run win for the Gold Coast.[[12]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nigeria_national_cricket_team#cite_note-13)

Matches resumed after the war with a five-day match in [Lagos](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lagos "Lagos") in 1947 which ended in a draw.[[13]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nigeria_national_cricket_team#cite_note-14) The 1949 match went the way of the Gold Coast.[[14]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nigeria_national_cricket_team#cite_note-15) As the number of Europeans working in the country reduced, the quality of the African players increased and cricket began to be organised on multi-racial lines in 1956.[[6]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nigeria_national_cricket_team#cite_note-EWC-7)

### Post independence

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Nigeria_national_cricket_team&action=edit&section=3 "Edit section: Post independence")]

[![Image 17](https://thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/3/3a/National_U-17_Championship_5th_Edition.jpg/250px-National_U-17_Championship_5th_Edition.jpg?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:National_U-17_Championship_5th_Edition.jpg)

National U-17 Championship, Northeast Edition (elimination), 2024 

Following Nigeria's independence in 1960, there was much interest in cricket. Annual matches against [Sierra Leone](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sierra_Leone_national_cricket_team "Sierra Leone national cricket team") and [The Gambia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gambia_national_cricket_team "Gambia national cricket team") began in 1964, and were evenly contested until the late 1970s, when [football](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Association_football "Association football") began to become more popular in the country. Cricket began a process of decline, and when [Tanzania](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tanzania_national_cricket_team "Tanzania national cricket team") toured in 1974, Nigeria lost two of the three matches and drew the other. They also lost heavily to the [MCC](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Marylebone_Cricket_Club "Marylebone Cricket Club") in 1976. Internal problems with both the Nigeria Cricket Association and in Nigeria itself led to a decline in standards, though Nigeria formed a majority of the players on the [West Africa cricket team](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/West_Africa_cricket_team "West Africa cricket team")[[6]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nigeria_national_cricket_team#cite_note-EWC-7) that became an ICC associate member in 1976.[[15]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nigeria_national_cricket_team#cite_note-16)

The West Africa team took part in the [ICC Trophy](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/ICC_Trophy "ICC Trophy") tournaments of [1982](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1982_ICC_Trophy "1982 ICC Trophy") and [1997](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1997_ICC_Trophy "1997 ICC Trophy") before withdrawing from the [2001 tournament](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2001_ICC_Trophy "2001 ICC Trophy") in Ontario.[[16]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nigeria_national_cricket_team#cite_note-17) Nigeria still continued to play on their own on occasion,[[6]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nigeria_national_cricket_team#cite_note-EWC-7) though they sometimes withdrew from tournaments, as at the 1998 Africa Cricket Association Championship.[[17]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nigeria_national_cricket_team#cite_note-18) The West African Cricket Conference ceased to exist in 2002,[[6]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nigeria_national_cricket_team#cite_note-EWC-7) and Nigeria became an associate member of the ICC in their own right the same year.[[9]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nigeria_national_cricket_team#cite_note-CAP-10)

### ICC membership

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Nigeria_national_cricket_team&action=edit&section=4 "Edit section: ICC membership")]

Nigeria's first tournament after becoming an ICC member on their own was the 2002 Africa Cup in [Zambia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Zambia "Zambia"). Nigeria finished fourth in their group after their only win of the tournament against [Malawi](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Malawi_national_cricket_team "Malawi national cricket team").[[18]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nigeria_national_cricket_team#cite_note-19) They finished 5th in the Africa Cricket Association Championships in 2004, their only win coming against the last-placed Tanzania, thus failing to qualify for the [2005 ICC Trophy](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2005_ICC_Trophy "2005 ICC Trophy").[[19]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nigeria_national_cricket_team#cite_note-ICCT05-20)

In August 2006, Nigeria took part in Division Two of the [World Cricket League Africa Region](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/World_Cricket_League_Africa_Region "World Cricket League Africa Region") in Tanzania,[[20]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nigeria_national_cricket_team#cite_note-21) finishing last.[[21]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nigeria_national_cricket_team#cite_note-WCLAfr2-22) This originally relegated them to Division Three,[[6]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nigeria_national_cricket_team#cite_note-EWC-7) though they are not playing in that tournament in 2008.[[22]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nigeria_national_cricket_team#cite_note-WCLA308-23) They won the North West Africa Championship in 2007[[23]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nigeria_national_cricket_team#cite_note-NWAC07-24) and 2008.[[24]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nigeria_national_cricket_team#cite_note-NWAC08-25) Nigeria played in Division Two of the World Cricket League Africa Region in 2008 and came second hence qualifying for [2009 ICC World Cricket League Division Seven](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2009_ICC_World_Cricket_League_Division_Seven "2009 ICC World Cricket League Division Seven"). They came 3rd in the tournament thus remaining in the division .[[22]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nigeria_national_cricket_team#cite_note-WCLA308-23) In May 2011 Nigeria participated in the [2011 ICC World Cricket League Division Seven](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2011_ICC_World_Cricket_League_Division_Seven "2011 ICC World Cricket League Division Seven") in Botswana.[[25]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nigeria_national_cricket_team#cite_note-26) Nigeria came second in tournament, thus qualifying for [2011 ICC World Cricket League Division Six](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2011_ICC_World_Cricket_League_Division_Six "2011 ICC World Cricket League Division Six"). Then the team went to South Africa in May 2011 to participate in 2011 ICC Africa Division Two (T20) en route to qualification of [2012 ICC World Twenty20](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2012_ICC_World_Twenty20 "2012 ICC World Twenty20"). They won the tournament and qualified for 2011 ICC Africa Division One.[[26]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nigeria_national_cricket_team#cite_note-cricketeurope4.net-27)

In August 2018, they were included in the [2018 Africa T20 Cup](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2018_Africa_T20_Cup "2018 Africa T20 Cup") tournament.[[27]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nigeria_national_cricket_team#cite_note-expand-28)[[28]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nigeria_national_cricket_team#cite_note-ICC-29)

### 2018–present

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Nigeria_national_cricket_team&action=edit&section=5 "Edit section: 2018–present")]

In April 2018, the ICC decided to grant full [Twenty20 International](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Twenty20_International "Twenty20 International") (T20I) status to all its members. Therefore, all [Twenty20](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Twenty20 "Twenty20") matches played between Nigeria and other [ICC members](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_International_Cricket_Council_members "List of International Cricket Council members") since 1 January 2019 have the T20I status.[[29]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nigeria_national_cricket_team#cite_note-30) Nigeria's first T20I match was against [Kenya](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kenya_national_cricket_team "Kenya national cricket team") on 20 May 2019, after finishing second in the [North-Western sub-region](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2018%E2%80%9319_ICC_World_Twenty20_Africa_Qualifier#North-Western_sub_region "2018–19 ICC World Twenty20 Africa Qualifier") qualification group, advancing to the Regional Final of the [2018–19 ICC World Twenty20 Africa Qualifier](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2018%E2%80%9319_ICC_World_Twenty20_Africa_Qualifier "2018–19 ICC World Twenty20 Africa Qualifier") tournament.[[30]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nigeria_national_cricket_team#cite_note-GhaNgr-31)

The **Namibia****men's national cricket team** represents [Namibia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Namibia "Namibia") in [international cricket](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/International_cricket "International cricket"). It is administered by [Cricket Namibia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cricket_Namibia "Cricket Namibia"), the governing body of cricket in Namibia, which has been an [associate member](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_International_Cricket_Council_members "List of International Cricket Council members") of the [International Cricket Council](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/International_Cricket_Council "International Cricket Council") since 1992.

A team representing [South West Africa](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/South_West_Africa "South West Africa") played in South African domestic competitions prior to Namibia's independence in 1990. After joining the ICC, the country soon became one of the leading ICC associate members in Africa. Namibia finished second at the [2001 ICC Trophy](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2001_ICC_Trophy "2001 ICC Trophy"), thereby qualifying for the [2003 Cricket World Cup](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2003_Cricket_World_Cup "2003 Cricket World Cup") in South Africa. The team made its [One Day International](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/One_Day_International "One Day International") (ODI) debut at the tournament but failed to win a match. Beginning in 2004, Namibia participated in every edition of the [ICC Intercontinental Cup](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/ICC_Intercontinental_Cup "ICC Intercontinental Cup"), finishing runners-up [in 2007–08](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2007%E2%80%9308_ICC_Intercontinental_Cup "2007–08 ICC Intercontinental Cup"). It also featured at the highest levels of the [World Cricket League](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/World_Cricket_League "World Cricket League") (WCL), twice participating in the [WCL Championship](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/ICC_World_Cricket_League_Championship "ICC World Cricket League Championship"), and finished third at the [2012 ICC World Twenty20 Qualifier](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2012_ICC_World_Twenty20_Qualifier "2012 ICC World Twenty20 Qualifier").

Namibia were runners-up at the [2019 WCL Division Two](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2019_ICC_World_Cricket_League_Division_Two "2019 ICC World Cricket League Division Two") tournament to secure the [ODI](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/One_Day_International "One Day International") status and qualify for the [2019–2023 ICC Cricket World Cup League 2](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2019%E2%80%932023_ICC_Cricket_World_Cup_League_2 "2019–2023 ICC Cricket World Cup League 2"). The team finished fourth at the [2019 ICC Men's T20 World Cup Qualifier](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2019_ICC_Men's_T20_World_Cup_Qualifier "2019 ICC Men's T20 World Cup Qualifier") to qualify for the [2021 ICC Men's T20 World Cup](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2021_ICC_Men's_T20_World_Cup "2021 ICC Men's T20 World Cup"). It subsequently recorded its first World Cup victories, defeating the [Netherlands](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Netherlands_national_cricket_team "Netherlands national cricket team") and [Ireland](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ireland_national_cricket_team "Ireland national cricket team") in the first round of the tournament to progress to the Super 12 stage.

## History

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Namibia_national_cricket_team&action=edit&section=1 "Edit section: History")]

The earliest instance of cricket being played in [Windhoek](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Windhoek "Windhoek") dates back to 1909 when [South West Africa](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/South_West_Africa "South West Africa") was very much a German colony.[[6]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Namibia_national_cricket_team#cite_note-7) During the [First World War](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/First_World_War "First World War") (1914), South African troops opened assault in the region. A game of cricket was recorded in the Okonjande prisoner of war camp near Otjiwarongo.[[7]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Namibia_national_cricket_team#cite_note-8) South Africa captured [South West Africa](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/South_West_Africa "South West Africa") following Germany's defeat. It came under the [League of Nations](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/League_of_Nations_mandate "League of Nations mandate") mandate in the [Union of South Africa](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Union_of_South_Africa "Union of South Africa").

Following this, cricket was regularly played in the Western Province. The South West Africa Cricket Union was formed in 1930 and the first organised matches were played in the region.[[8]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Namibia_national_cricket_team#cite_note-9)[South West Africa](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/South_West_Africa "South West Africa") began playing in the South African Country Cricket Association's annual competition in the 1961–62 season.[[9]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Namibia_national_cricket_team#cite_note-SA-10)

### South West Africa (1961–1989)

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Namibia_national_cricket_team&action=edit&section=2 "Edit section: South West Africa (1961–1989)")]

[South West Africa](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/South_West_Africa "South West Africa") competed in the South African Country Cricket Association's annual competition between 1961 and 1989.[[9]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Namibia_national_cricket_team#cite_note-SA-10) In 1966, the [Namibian war of Independence](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/South_African_Border_War "South African Border War") was launched by the [People's Liberation Army of Namibia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/People's_Liberation_Army_of_Namibia "People's Liberation Army of Namibia"), an armed wing of [SWAPO](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/SWAPO "SWAPO"). South West African rebels welcomed the sporting boycott of the South African apartheid regime and lent their support to the "Stop the seventy tour" campaign.

South West Africa played their last domestic season in South Africa in January 1989. In April, [PLAN](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/People's_Liberation_Army_of_Namibia "People's Liberation Army of Namibia") launched its [final guerrilla campaign](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Operation_Merlyn "Operation Merlyn") and the South West Africa Cricket Union severed their ties with the South African Cricket Board (SACB).

In November 1989, a Namibian team toured Botswana and played their first international fixture,[[10]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Namibia_national_cricket_team#cite_note-11) although the [Namibian Cricket Board](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cricket_Namibia "Cricket Namibia") were not affiliated to the [International Cricket Council](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/International_Cricket_Council "International Cricket Council") until 1992.[[11]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Namibia_national_cricket_team#cite_note-NamCA-12)

### Initial years

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Namibia_national_cricket_team&action=edit&section=3 "Edit section: Initial years")]

After the Botswana tour, [Gloucestershire County Cricket Club](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gloucestershire_County_Cricket_Club "Gloucestershire County Cricket Club") visited Namibia in March 1990, taking part in the Independence Day celebrations.[[12]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Namibia_national_cricket_team#cite_note-13) This was followed by a visit from [The Netherlands](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Netherlands_national_cricket_team "Netherlands national cricket team") in April.[[13]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Namibia_national_cricket_team#cite_note-14) Before the formation of the [African Cricket Association](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/African_Cricket_Association "African Cricket Association"), the SCSA Zone VI cricket federation was formed after two schoolboy cricket tours between Namibia and Botswana in 1989 and 1990.[[14]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Namibia_national_cricket_team#cite_note-audiodata.cricinfo.com-15) The inaugural ACA tournament was held in Windhoek in September 1991, with Zambia, Malawi, Namibia, Lesotho and Botswana playing as well as an [Oxford University Cricket Club](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Oxford_University_Cricket_Club "Oxford University Cricket Club") side.[[14]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Namibia_national_cricket_team#cite_note-audiodata.cricinfo.com-15)

### 2003 World Cup

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Namibia_national_cricket_team&action=edit&section=4 "Edit section: 2003 World Cup")]

The road to the [2003 Cricket World Cup](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2003_Cricket_World_Cup "2003 Cricket World Cup") started with the [2001 ICC Trophy](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2001_ICC_Trophy "2001 ICC Trophy") in Canada. Namibia reached the final at the [Toronto Cricket, Skating and Curling Club](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Toronto_Cricket,_Skating_and_Curling_Club "Toronto Cricket, Skating and Curling Club"), losing to the Netherlands, but still qualifying for their first World Cup.[[15]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Namibia_national_cricket_team#cite_note-ICCT01-16) Namibia then hosted the [ICC 6 Nations Challenge](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/ICC_6_Nations_Challenge "ICC 6 Nations Challenge") in April 2002, finishing fourth[[16]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Namibia_national_cricket_team#cite_note-ICC6N02-17) and had a disappointing Africa Cup campaign that September, finishing fourth in their group and beating only [Tanzania](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tanzania_national_cricket_team "Tanzania national cricket team"),[[17]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Namibia_national_cricket_team#cite_note-18) before losing four matches against Zimbabwe A a few weeks later.[[18]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Namibia_national_cricket_team#cite_note-19) A tour of Kenya was more successful, as Namibia beat [Kenya](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kenya_national_cricket_team "Kenya national cricket team") in a four match one-day series.[[19]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Namibia_national_cricket_team#cite_note-20) Following this, Namibia took part in the top level of South African domestic one-day cricket, the Standard Bank Cup, but lost all five of their games.[[20]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Namibia_national_cricket_team#cite_note-21) Bangladesh toured in January 2003, winning the five match one-day series 4–1.[[21]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Namibia_national_cricket_team#cite_note-22)

The World Cup itself started on 10 February 2003 in [Harare](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Harare "Harare") with [Zimbabwe](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Zimbabwe_national_cricket_team "Zimbabwe national cricket team") beating Namibia by 86 runs in Namibia's debut [One Day International](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/One_Day_International "One Day International") (ODI).[[22]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Namibia_national_cricket_team#cite_note-23)

They went on to lose to [Pakistan](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pakistan_national_cricket_team "Pakistan national cricket team") by 171 runs,[[23]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Namibia_national_cricket_team#cite_note-24) before a 55 run defeat at the hands of [England](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/England_national_cricket_team "England national cricket team") in which Namibia performed with some credit, [Jan-Berrie Burger](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jan-Berrie_Burger "Jan-Berrie Burger") winning the [man of the match](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Man_of_the_match "Man of the match") award for his innings of 85 runs that came close to helping the side pull off an unlikely upset.[[24]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Namibia_national_cricket_team#cite_note-25) They then lost by 181 runs to [India](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/India_national_cricket_team "India national cricket team")[[25]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Namibia_national_cricket_team#cite_note-26) and by 256 runs against [Australia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Australia_national_cricket_team "Australia national cricket team"),[[26]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Namibia_national_cricket_team#cite_note-27) the eventual winners of the tournament,[[27]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Namibia_national_cricket_team#cite_note-WC03-28) in what at the time was the biggest winning margin in One Day Internationals.[[28]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Namibia_national_cricket_team#cite_note-29) The tournament finished with a 64 run loss to fellow qualifiers the Netherlands.[[29]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Namibia_national_cricket_team#cite_note-30)

### After the World Cup

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Namibia_national_cricket_team&action=edit&section=5 "Edit section: After the World Cup")]

In August 2003, Zimbabwe A toured Namibia. Namibia won the one-day series 2–1, but lost both three-day games.[[30]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Namibia_national_cricket_team#cite_note-31) A return visit to Zimbabwe the following January saw Namibia win a five match one-day series against Zimbabwe A 4–1, also winning a match against Zimbabwe Under-19s.[[31]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Namibia_national_cricket_team#cite_note-32) Bangladesh toured Namibia in February, winning all three one-day games and drawing the three-day game.[[32]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Namibia_national_cricket_team#cite_note-33) Following this, Namibia travelled to the United Arab Emirates for the [2004 ICC Six Nations Challenge](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2004_ICC_Six_Nations_Challenge "2004 ICC Six Nations Challenge"). They finished third on run rate after beating [Canada](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Canada_national_cricket_team "Canada national cricket team"), the Netherlands and the [UAE](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/United_Arab_Emirates_national_cricket_team "United Arab Emirates national cricket team") and losing to Scotland and the [USA](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/United_States_national_cricket_team "United States national cricket team").[[33]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Namibia_national_cricket_team#cite_note-ICC6N04-34) Namibia played two [ICC Intercontinental Cup](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/ICC_Intercontinental_Cup "ICC Intercontinental Cup") matches against Kenya and [Uganda](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Uganda_national_cricket_team "Uganda national cricket team") in 2004, losing them both.[[34]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Namibia_national_cricket_team#cite_note-ICCup04-35) In between the two matches, they won an African nations tournament in Zambia.[[35]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Namibia_national_cricket_team#cite_note-36) Later in the year, they took part in Zimbabwe's national one-day domestic competition, in which they finished as runners-up.[[36]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Namibia_national_cricket_team#cite_note-37) Whilst in Zimbabwe, they won two matches against the national side.[[37]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Namibia_national_cricket_team#cite_note-38) This was followed by a visit to Namibia by England, who won both matches.[[38]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Namibia_national_cricket_team#cite_note-39)

Zimbabwe A again visited Namibia in early 2005, losing both one-day matches that finished.[[39]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Namibia_national_cricket_team#cite_note-40) Pakistan A were the next visitors in April, winning all three one-day matches and drawing in the three-day game.[[40]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Namibia_national_cricket_team#cite_note-41) This was followed by their two regional group games in the [2005 ICC Intercontinental Cup](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2005_ICC_Intercontinental_Cup "2005 ICC Intercontinental Cup"). Whilst they were unbeaten, winning against Uganda and drawing against Kenya, this was not enough to qualify for the semi-finals.[[41]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Namibia_national_cricket_team#cite_note-ICCup05-42) They then visited Ireland to take part in the [2005 ICC Trophy](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2005_ICC_Trophy "2005 ICC Trophy"). They finished 7th after beating Denmark in their final play-off game.[[42]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Namibia_national_cricket_team#cite_note-ICCT05-43) Back at home, they hosted [New Zealand](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/New_Zealand_national_cricket_team "New Zealand national cricket team") at the end of July, losing both games,[[43]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Namibia_national_cricket_team#cite_note-44) losing by only 29 runs after conceding 330/6.[[44]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Namibia_national_cricket_team#cite_note-45) In October of that year, they hosted the semi-finals of the Intercontinental Cup, despite failing to qualify. While the final was being played, they played a two match one-day series against Bermuda after they had been knocked out of the tournament, winning both games, but the games were tarnished by controversial incidents, with the Bermuda team accusing the Namibian team of racist insults, and walking off in the second game when a flurry of [bouncers](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bouncer_(cricket) "Bouncer (cricket)") were unleashed at the lower order Bermuda batsmen.[[45]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Namibia_national_cricket_team#cite_note-46) The Namibian Cricket Board denied the allegations of racism.[[46]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Namibia_national_cricket_team#cite_note-47)

In March 2006, Namibia met [Nepal](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nepal_national_cricket_team "Nepal national cricket team") in a challenge match to decide who got the eighth and final spot in the [2006 ICC Intercontinental Cup](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2006_ICC_Intercontinental_Cup "2006 ICC Intercontinental Cup"). The match was drawn, with Namibia getting a first innings lead, thus qualifying them for the main tournament. The main tournament itself started with an innings defeat by Scotland in [Aberdeen](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Aberdeen "Aberdeen") before a five wicket defeat by [Ireland](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ireland_cricket_team "Ireland cricket team") in Dublin, both matches in May.[[47]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Namibia_national_cricket_team#cite_note-ICCup06-48) In the [2006–07 South African cricket season](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2006%E2%80%9307_South_African_cricket_season "2006–07 South African cricket season"), Namibia took part in the second tier of [first-class](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/First-class_cricket "First-class cricket") and [List A cricket](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_A_cricket "List A cricket"), the South African Airways Challenge. They finished second in their group in the three-day tournament[[48]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Namibia_national_cricket_team#cite_note-49) and third in their group in the one-day tournament, missing out on reaching the semi-finals by one win.[[49]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Namibia_national_cricket_team#cite_note-50) In the midst of the matches in those tournaments, they played their third and final 2006 Intercontinental Cup match, beating the UAE by an innings.[[47]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Namibia_national_cricket_team#cite_note-ICCup06-48) On 1 April 2007, they became part of the ICC's High Performance Program.[[50]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Namibia_national_cricket_team#cite_note-HPP-51)

In November/December 2007, Namibia hosted [Division Two](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2007_ICC_World_Cricket_League_Division_Two "2007 ICC World Cricket League Division Two") of the [World Cricket League](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/World_Cricket_League "World Cricket League") where they played against [Argentina](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Argentina_national_cricket_team "Argentina national cricket team"), [Denmark](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Danish_cricket_team "Danish cricket team"), [Oman](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Oman_national_cricket_team "Oman national cricket team"), [the UAE](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/United_Arab_Emirates_cricket_team "United Arab Emirates cricket team") and [Uganda](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ugandan_cricket_team "Ugandan cricket team"). Although Namibia won three of their five group matches, it was not enough for them to progress to the final. Namibia beat Denmark in the third place playoff. On the basis of their top four finish in this tournament, Namibia qualified for the [ICC World Cup Qualifier](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/ICC_World_Cup_Qualifier "ICC World Cup Qualifier") in 2009, the final tournament in qualification for the [2011 World Cup](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2011_Cricket_World_Cup "2011 Cricket World Cup").

Namibia again took part in the second tier of South African domestic cricket between October 2007 and February 2008.[[51]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Namibia_national_cricket_team#cite_note-52) They played a [2007–08 ICC Intercontinental Cup](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2007%E2%80%9308_ICC_Intercontinental_Cup "2007–08 ICC Intercontinental Cup") match against Canada in October 2007, playing the remaining games against Bermuda, Ireland, Kenya, the Netherlands, Scotland and the UAE in 2008.[[52]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Namibia_national_cricket_team#cite_note-ICCup08-53)

Namibia won the [2009–10 ICC Intercontinental Shield](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2009%E2%80%9310_ICC_Intercontinental_Shield "2009–10 ICC Intercontinental Shield") defeating the [United Arab Emirates](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/United_Arab_Emirates_national_cricket_team "United Arab Emirates national cricket team") by six wickets in Dubai.[[53]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Namibia_national_cricket_team#cite_note-54) In 2011 Namibia participated in [Division Two](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2011_ICC_World_Cricket_League_Division_Two "2011 ICC World Cricket League Division Two") and finished as runners-up, on this occasion behind the UAE.[[54]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Namibia_national_cricket_team#cite_note-55)

In July 2011, the country competed in the ICC Twenty20 World Cricket League Africa Division One competition in Uganda, winning all eight group matches before succumbing to the [hosts](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Uganda_national_cricket_team "Uganda national cricket team") in the Final by six wickets.[[55]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Namibia_national_cricket_team#cite_note-56) During this tournament, all-rounder Louis van der Westhuizen struck 16 sixes in an innings of 159* against Kenya, as part of a team total of 262/1 from 20 overs.

Namibia are participating in the inaugural [2023 Cricket World Cup Qualifier Play-off](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2023_Cricket_World_Cup_Qualifier_Play-off "2023 Cricket World Cup Qualifier Play-off"), a part of the qualification process for [2023 Cricket World Cup](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2023_Cricket_World_Cup "2023 Cricket World Cup"), as the hosts.[[63]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Namibia_national_cricket_team#cite_note-64) They got their maiden win in the tournament against [Papua New Guinea](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Papua_New_Guinea_national_cricket_team "Papua New Guinea national cricket team"), as they won the match by 48 runs.[[64]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Namibia_national_cricket_team#cite_note-65) Namibia's score of 381/8 was the highest total by an [associate nation](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_International_Cricket_Council_members#Associate_Members "List of International Cricket Council members") in an ODI match.[[65]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Namibia_national_cricket_team#cite_note-66)

The [South African cricket team](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/South_Africa_national_cricket_team "South Africa national cricket team") toured Namibia in October 2025 for a one-off [Twenty20 International](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Twenty20_International "Twenty20 International") (T20I) match to inaugurate the opening of Cricket Namibia's first official stadium, the [Namibia Cricket Ground](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Namibia_Cricket_Ground "Namibia Cricket Ground") in [Windhoek](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Windhoek "Windhoek").[[66]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Namibia_national_cricket_team#cite_note-67)[[67]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Namibia_national_cricket_team#cite_note-68) It was the first-ever international match between the two sides.[[68]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Namibia_national_cricket_team#cite_note-69) Namibia won the match by 4 wickets in a last ball thrilling upset.[[69]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Namibia_national_cricket_team#cite_note-70)[[70]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Namibia_national_cricket_team#cite_note-71)

The **Kyambogo Cricket Oval** is a [cricket](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cricket "Cricket") ground in [Kampala](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kampala "Kampala"), [Uganda](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Uganda "Uganda").[[1]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kyambogo_Cricket_Oval#cite_note-1) It hosted matches in the [2017 ICC World Cricket League Division Three](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2017_ICC_World_Cricket_League_Division_Three "2017 ICC World Cricket League Division Three") tournament,[[2]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kyambogo_Cricket_Oval#cite_note-2) as well as in the [Regional Finals](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2018%E2%80%9319_ICC_World_Twenty20_Africa_Qualifier#Regional_Finals "2018–19 ICC World Twenty20 Africa Qualifier") of the [2018–19 ICC World Twenty20 Africa Qualifier](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2018%E2%80%9319_ICC_World_Twenty20_Africa_Qualifier "2018–19 ICC World Twenty20 Africa Qualifier") tournament in May 2019.[[3]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kyambogo_Cricket_Oval#cite_note-3)

The **Kenya men's national cricket team** represents the [Republic of Kenya](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Republic_of_Kenya "Republic of Kenya") in [international cricket](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/International_cricket "International cricket"). Kenya is an associate member of the [International Cricket Council](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/International_Cricket_Council "International Cricket Council") (ICC) which has [Twenty20 International](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Twenty20_International "Twenty20 International") (T20I) status after the ICC granted T20I status to all its members.[[7]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kenya_national_cricket_team#cite_note-International_Cricket_Council-8)

They have been an [associate member](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_International_Cricket_Council_members "List of International Cricket Council members") of the ICC since 1981. Since then they have played in five [Cricket World Cups](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cricket_World_Cup "Cricket World Cup") from 1996 to 2011 with their best result being a bronze medal finish as the semi-final appearance at the [2003 Cricket World Cup](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2003_Cricket_World_Cup "2003 Cricket World Cup") in Southern Africa. They have only qualified for one [ICC World Twenty20](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/ICC_World_Twenty20 "ICC World Twenty20") tournament, in [2007](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2007_ICC_World_Twenty20 "2007 ICC World Twenty20"). The Kenyan national team is governed by [Cricket Kenya](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cricket_Kenya "Cricket Kenya").

Kenya gained [One Day International](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/One_Day_International "One Day International") (ODI) status in 1996 in preparation for the [1996 Cricket World Cup](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1996_Cricket_World_Cup "1996 Cricket World Cup") and would have it for eighteen years before losing it at the [2014 Cricket World Cup Qualifier](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2014_Cricket_World_Cup_Qualifier "2014 Cricket World Cup Qualifier") where they finished in the fifth place. Recently they competed in the African Continental and emerged winners of the 2026 edition, this is their first title since the inauguration of the tournament[[8]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kenya_national_cricket_team#cite_note-9). Kenya is set to play the qualifiers round for the upcoming 2028 T20 World Cup after being promoted from the sub regional round.[[9]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kenya_national_cricket_team#cite_note-10)

## History

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Kenya_national_cricket_team&action=edit&section=2 "Edit section: History")]

### East Africa team

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Kenya_national_cricket_team&action=edit&section=3 "Edit section: East Africa team")]

_Full article: [East Africa cricket team](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/East\_Africa\_cricket\_team "East Africa cricket team")_
Kenya, [Tanzania](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tanzania "Tanzania") and [Uganda](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Uganda "Uganda") combined to form the East Africa cricket team, which became an associate member of the ICC in 1966.[[10]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kenya_national_cricket_team#cite_note-11) They continued playing amongst themselves, and were joined by [Zambia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Zambia_national_cricket_team "Zambia national cricket team") in a quadrangular tournament played annually between 1966 and 1980.[[11]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kenya_national_cricket_team#cite_note-Hist-12)

[India](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/India_national_cricket_team "India national cricket team") toured East Africa in 1967[[12]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kenya_national_cricket_team#cite_note-13) and played a three-day match against Kenya on 5 August, which was drawn.[[13]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kenya_national_cricket_team#cite_note-14) Various tours of, and by, East Africa continued, including a tour of [England](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/England "England") in 1972[[14]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kenya_national_cricket_team#cite_note-15) and a [first-class](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/First-class_cricket "First-class cricket") match between East Africa and the [MCC](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Marylebone_Cricket_Club "Marylebone Cricket Club") at [Nairobi Gymkhana Club](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gymkhana_Club_Ground "Gymkhana Club Ground") in 1974[[15]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kenya_national_cricket_team#cite_note-16) before East Africa took part in the first [Cricket World Cup](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cricket_World_Cup "Cricket World Cup").

The [1975 Cricket World Cup](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1975_Cricket_World_Cup "1975 Cricket World Cup") took place in England, and East Africa was one of two non-test teams invited to the tournament, the other being [Sri Lanka](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sri_Lanka_national_cricket_team "Sri Lanka national cricket team").[[16]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kenya_national_cricket_team#cite_note-WC75-17) Kenya provided half of the fourteen-man squad for the tournament.[[11]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kenya_national_cricket_team#cite_note-Hist-12) After warm-up matches against [Somerset](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Somerset_County_Cricket_Club "Somerset County Cricket Club"), [Wales](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wales_national_cricket_team "Wales national cricket team"), [Glamorgan](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Glamorgan_County_Cricket_Club "Glamorgan County Cricket Club") and various club teams, they played in the same first round group as [England](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/England_cricket_team "England cricket team"), [India](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/India_national_cricket_team "India national cricket team") and [New Zealand](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/New_Zealand_national_cricket_team "New Zealand national cricket team"), losing to all three.[[16]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kenya_national_cricket_team#cite_note-WC75-17) The World Cup was followed by a first-class match against Sri Lanka at the [County Ground, Taunton](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/County_Ground,_Taunton "County Ground, Taunton").[[17]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kenya_national_cricket_team#cite_note-18)

East Africa then took part in the [1979 ICC Trophy](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1979_ICC_Trophy "1979 ICC Trophy"), the first [ICC Trophy](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cricket_World_Cup_Qualifier "Cricket World Cup Qualifier") tournament, but did not progress beyond the first round, thus missing out on qualification for the [1979 World Cup](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1979_Cricket_World_Cup "1979 Cricket World Cup").[[18]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kenya_national_cricket_team#cite_note-ICC79-19)

### ICC membership

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Kenya_national_cricket_team&action=edit&section=4 "Edit section: ICC membership")]

Long considered the strongest part of the [East African cricket team](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/East_Africa_cricket_team "East Africa cricket team"),[[11]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kenya_national_cricket_team#cite_note-Hist-12) Kenya broke away in 1981 and joined the ICC in their own right as an associate member,[[19]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kenya_national_cricket_team#cite_note-20) shortly after a tour of [Zimbabwe](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Zimbabwe "Zimbabwe") in 1980/81. They played two three-day matches against [Zimbabwe](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Zimbabwe_national_cricket_team "Zimbabwe national cricket team") on that tour, losing both.[[20]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kenya_national_cricket_team#cite_note-21) Kenya played in the ICC Trophy in their own right in [1982](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1982_ICC_Trophy "1982 ICC Trophy"),[[21]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kenya_national_cricket_team#cite_note-ICC82-22)[1986](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1986_ICC_Trophy "1986 ICC Trophy"),[[22]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kenya_national_cricket_team#cite_note-ICC86-23) and [1990](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1990_ICC_Trophy "1990 ICC Trophy"),[[23]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kenya_national_cricket_team#cite_note-ICC90-24) also playing their first first-class match against [Pakistan B](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pakistan_national_cricket_team "Pakistan national cricket team") in September 1986.[[24]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kenya_national_cricket_team#cite_note-25)

### 1996 World Cup

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Kenya_national_cricket_team&action=edit&section=5 "Edit section: 1996 World Cup")]

The [1994 ICC Trophy](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1994_ICC_Trophy "1994 ICC Trophy") was hosted in [Nairobi](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nairobi "Nairobi") and Kenya finished as runners-up to the [UAE](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/United_Arab_Emirates_national_cricket_team "United Arab Emirates national cricket team"), thus qualifying for the [1996 World Cup](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1996_Cricket_World_Cup "1996 Cricket World Cup").[[25]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kenya_national_cricket_team#cite_note-ICC94-26) Kenya then played at home against India A in August 1995,[[26]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kenya_national_cricket_team#cite_note-27) and went on a tour to [South Africa](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/South_Africa "South Africa") in September/October that year,[[27]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kenya_national_cricket_team#cite_note-28) before playing in the World Cup, which was to bring Kenyan cricket to a much wider audience, and catapult them into the spotlight.

Kenya was in the same group as [Australia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Australia_national_cricket_team "Australia national cricket team"), India, Sri Lanka, the [West Indies](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/West_Indies_cricket_team "West Indies cricket team") and Zimbabwe.[[28]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kenya_national_cricket_team#cite_note-WC96-29) They played their very first ODI match against India.

### 2003 World Cup and decline

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Kenya_national_cricket_team&action=edit&section=7 "Edit section: 2003 World Cup and decline")]

The [2003 Cricket World Cup](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2003_Cricket_World_Cup "2003 Cricket World Cup") was to be Kenya's finest moment in international cricket to date. The tournament was held in South Africa, with Kenya hosting their two matches against Sri Lanka and New Zealand.[[61]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kenya_national_cricket_team#cite_note-62) The tournament started with a defeat to South Africa,[[62]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kenya_national_cricket_team#cite_note-63) but Kenya bounced back with a four wicket win over Canada in [Cape Town](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cape_Town "Cape Town").[[63]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kenya_national_cricket_team#cite_note-64) New Zealand forfeited their match against Kenya in Nairobi due to safety concerns,[[64]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kenya_national_cricket_team#cite_note-65) but Sri Lanka did visit Nairobi and much to their dismay lost by 53 runs as Kenya pulled off another upset victory.[[65]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kenya_national_cricket_team#cite_note-66)

The tournament continued, back in South Africa, with a win over Bangladesh[[66]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kenya_national_cricket_team#cite_note-67) and a defeat to the West Indies.[[67]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kenya_national_cricket_team#cite_note-68) Kenya had done enough to qualify for the Super Six stage, becoming the first non-test nation to progress beyond the first round of the World Cup. In the Super Six stage, they lost to India[[68]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kenya_national_cricket_team#cite_note-69) and Australia,[[69]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kenya_national_cricket_team#cite_note-70) but beat Zimbabwe by seven wickets,[[70]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kenya_national_cricket_team#cite_note-71) qualifying for the semi-final, where they lost to India by 91 runs.[[71]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kenya_national_cricket_team#cite_note-WC03SF-72)

Kenya's World Cup success was rewarded with a spot in a quadrangular tournament at the [Sharjah Cricket Association Stadium](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sharjah_Cricket_Stadium "Sharjah Cricket Stadium") against Pakistan, Sri Lanka and Zimbabwe, but they lost all three of their games.[[72]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kenya_national_cricket_team#cite_note-73)

Kenya's failure in the above tournament is perhaps indicative of how they failed to capitalise on their World Cup success, though it must be said that not all of that failure was on the field. Although Kenya were given plenty of matches against national A teams, and played in the [Carib Beer Cup](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/West_Indies_Championship "West Indies Championship") in the [West Indies](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/West_Indies "West Indies") in 2004,[[73]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kenya_national_cricket_team#cite_note-74) Kenya only played two ODIs in the three years after the Sharjah tournament, against India and Pakistan in the [2004 ICC Champions Trophy](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2004_ICC_Champions_Trophy "2004 ICC Champions Trophy").[[74]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kenya_national_cricket_team#cite_note-CT04-75)

Off-field setbacks also occurred. [Maurice Odumbe](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Maurice_Odumbe "Maurice Odumbe") was banned for match-fixing in August 2004,[[75]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kenya_national_cricket_team#cite_note-76) and a series of strikes by players[[76]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kenya_national_cricket_team#cite_note-CIHist-77) led to a weakened Kenyan team being eliminated from the inaugural [ICC Intercontinental Cup](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/ICC_Intercontinental_Cup "ICC Intercontinental Cup") at the semi-final stage by Scotland.[[77]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kenya_national_cricket_team#cite_note-KenScoSF-78) By the end of the dispute in 2005, Kenyan cricket had no sponsors and was in virtual international isolation.[[76]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kenya_national_cricket_team#cite_note-CIHist-77) At that stage the governing body had dissolved internally and Kenyan cricket opportunities were limited and international cricket for them had virtually ceased.

### Rebuilding

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Kenya_national_cricket_team&action=edit&section=8 "Edit section: Rebuilding")]

#### 2005 to 2007

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Kenya_national_cricket_team&action=edit&section=9 "Edit section: 2005 to 2007")]

A rebuilding process began in 2005. The player strikes ceased, and Kenya again reached the semi-finals of the Intercontinental Cup. They warmed up for the semi-finals in Windhoek with a tour of Zimbabwe, to play two first-class and one one-day match against Zimbabwe A. They won all three of those games,[[78]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kenya_national_cricket_team#cite_note-KinZ0506-79) and drew against [Bermuda](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bermuda_national_cricket_team "Bermuda national cricket team") in the semi-final of the [2005 ICC Intercontinental Cup](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2005_ICC_Intercontinental_Cup "2005 ICC Intercontinental Cup")[[79]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kenya_national_cricket_team#cite_note-80) but lost to Ireland in the final, despite scoring 404/4 in their first innings.[[80]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kenya_national_cricket_team#cite_note-IreKenF-81)

In early 2006, the Kenya Cricket Association was disbanded and replaced by [Cricket Kenya](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cricket_Kenya "Cricket Kenya").[[76]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kenya_national_cricket_team#cite_note-CIHist-77) The rebuilding process was in full swing as Kenya began playing ODI cricket again. Their return to ODI cricket was a five match series against Zimbabwe, which was drawn 2–2 with one match abandoned.[[78]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kenya_national_cricket_team#cite_note-KinZ0506-79) This was followed by a four match ODI series against Bangladesh, with Kenya losing all four matches in that series.[[81]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kenya_national_cricket_team#cite_note-82) Their [2006 ICC Intercontinental Cup](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2006%E2%80%9307_ICC_Intercontinental_Cup "2006–07 ICC Intercontinental Cup") campaign got off to a poor start with a draw against the Netherlands[[82]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kenya_national_cricket_team#cite_note-83) and a defeat to Canada,[[83]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kenya_national_cricket_team#cite_note-84) but they bounced right back with two ODI wins over Canada at the [Toronto Cricket, Skating and Curling Club](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Toronto_Cricket,_Skating_and_Curling_Club "Toronto Cricket, Skating and Curling Club").[[84]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kenya_national_cricket_team#cite_note-85) Bangladesh toured Kenya in August, winning all three ODIs,[[85]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kenya_national_cricket_team#cite_note-86) before an Intercontinental Cup draw against Bermuda[[86]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kenya_national_cricket_team#cite_note-87) and three ODI wins over Bermuda.[[87]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kenya_national_cricket_team#cite_note-88)

A triangular tournament in [Mombasa](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mombasa "Mombasa") against Canada and Scotland began Kenya's 2007 and Kenya won the tournament.[[88]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kenya_national_cricket_team#cite_note-89) They then hosted [Division One](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2007_World_Cricket_League_Division_One "2007 World Cricket League Division One") of the [World Cricket League](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/World_Cricket_League "World Cricket League") at three grounds in Nairobi, playing against Bermuda, Canada, Ireland, the Netherlands and Scotland. Kenya also won this event, beating Scotland in the final.[[89]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kenya_national_cricket_team#cite_note-WCLD107-90) This was followed by the [2007 World Cup](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2007_Cricket_World_Cup "2007 Cricket World Cup"), Kenya's fourth World Cup. Kenya beat Canada in the first round, but lost to England and New Zealand, thus missing out on the Super Eight stage.[[90]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kenya_national_cricket_team#cite_note-WC07-91)

#### 2008 to 2011

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Kenya_national_cricket_team&action=edit&section=10 "Edit section: 2008 to 2011")]

In August 2008, after a break of nine months without a One Day or Twenty20 International, Kenya toured Ireland, Scotland and the Netherlands for various series. It proved a disappointing tour overall, with rain and poor Kenyan batting performances being the main themes.

Kenya initially participated in the [2009 ICC World Twenty20 Qualifier](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2008_World_Twenty20_Qualifier "2008 World Twenty20 Qualifier") in [Belfast](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Belfast "Belfast"), [Northern Ireland](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Northern_Ireland "Northern Ireland"), the associate qualification tournament for the [2009 ICC World Twenty20](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2009_World_Twenty20 "2009 World Twenty20"). One of the favourites at the start of the tournament, they finished second in Group B with a loss to the [Netherlands](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Netherlands_national_cricket_team "Netherlands national cricket team") and a win over [Canada](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Canada_national_cricket_team "Canada national cricket team"), but losses to [Ireland](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ireland_cricket_team "Ireland cricket team") and [Scotland](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Scotland_national_cricket_team "Scotland national cricket team") in the knock-out stages meant that they finished fourth and thus failed to qualify for the World Twenty20.

Kenya then participated in three ODI series across Europe, but these merely resulted in two wash-outs against [Scotland](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kenyan_cricket_team_in_Scotland_in_2008 "Kenyan cricket team in Scotland in 2008"), defeat in a rain-affected one-off match to the [Netherlands](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kenyan_cricket_team_in_the_Netherlands_in_2008 "Kenyan cricket team in the Netherlands in 2008"), and losing a three-match series against [Ireland](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kenyan_cricket_team_in_Ireland_in_2008 "Kenyan cricket team in Ireland in 2008") 1–0 with two matches affected by rain.

In October 2008, Kenya hosted Ireland and Zimbabwe in an [ODI series](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2008_Associates_Tri-Series_in_Kenya "2008 Associates Tri-Series in Kenya") in Nairobi, but after a loss to Ireland and a win over Zimbabwe, their last three matches were all abandoned due to rain.[[93]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kenya_national_cricket_team#cite_note-94) After this washed-out series, Kenya then travelled to [South Africa for two ODIs](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kenyan_cricket_team_in_South_Africa_in_2008%E2%80%9309 "Kenyan cricket team in South Africa in 2008–09"), losing heavily in both.[[94]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kenya_national_cricket_team#cite_note-95)

In late January and early February 2009, Kenya played [five ODIs at home against Zimbabwe](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Zimbabwean_cricket_team_in_Kenya_in_2008%E2%80%9309 "Zimbabwean cricket team in Kenya in 2008–09"), but lost all of them.[[95]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kenya_national_cricket_team#cite_note-96)

Since the World Cup, a team known as [Kenya Select](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kenya_Select "Kenya Select") has taken part in Zimbabwe's [Logan Cup](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Logan_Cup "Logan Cup") competition, but did not win a game,[[96]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kenya_national_cricket_team#cite_note-97) also losing to Zimbabwe A.[[97]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kenya_national_cricket_team#cite_note-98)

In their opening match of World Cup 2011 campaign, Kenya faced a mammoth defeat from New Zealand by 10 wickets, they were bowled out for 69 runs and New Zealand won the match in just 8 overs without the loss of a wicket.[[98]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kenya_national_cricket_team#cite_note-99)

In 2011, Kenya was whitewashed by the [Netherlands national cricket team](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Netherlands_national_cricket_team "Netherlands national cricket team") in a short 2 match ODI series played in Sportspark Westvielt, Voorburg. During this series, Kenya's weak batting was noted. They made only 208/8 in the first match and an even smaller 184/8 in the second match. [Seren Waters](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Seren_Waters "Seren Waters") and [Collins Obuya](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Collins_Obuya "Collins Obuya") (the national team captain) did, however, have notable performances – the former making 71 in the first match and the latter scoring 54 in the second match.

#### Reforms in 2011

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Kenya_national_cricket_team&action=edit&section=11 "Edit section: Reforms in 2011")]

For years, the Kenyan players had been the [Associate](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_International_Cricket_Council_members#Associate_and_Affiliate_Nations "List of International Cricket Council members") nations' most pampered professionals. The first time [Cricket Kenya](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cricket_Kenya "Cricket Kenya")'s notice was attracted was when during the [2011 ODI World Cup](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2011_Cricket_World_Cup "2011 Cricket World Cup"), there were reports of internal dissent between the team,[[99]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kenya_national_cricket_team#cite_note-100) as the team had a disastrous World Cup, losing all six of their games.[[100]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kenya_national_cricket_team#cite_note-101) Cricket Kenya announced that it would review the World Cup debacle after the tournament was over. This was the beginning of a series of reforms initiated by the board.[[101]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kenya_national_cricket_team#cite_note-102)

Following the reviews, the board replaced the former Sahara Elite League with the East African tournaments. While the [East Africa Premier League](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/East_Africa_Premier_League "East Africa Premier League") is a [Twenty20](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Twenty20 "Twenty20") tournament, the [East African Cup](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/East_Africa_Cup "East Africa Cup") is a 50-over tournament. It is currently hoped that this tournaments will produce further new young talents for Kenya in the future.[[102]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kenya_national_cricket_team#cite_note-103) Within months, the East African tournaments were regarded in high esteem and the intensity was up to the brink, as an [Cricinfo](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cricinfo "Cricinfo") interview with Cricket Kenya CEO Tom Sears revealed.[[103]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kenya_national_cricket_team#cite_note-104)

Another important reform brought in by the board was to dump the old guard. As described by Cricinfo journalist Martin Williamson, the old guard was not committed to performance and was more keen to selfish gains.[[104]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kenya_national_cricket_team#cite_note-105) The new contracts had completely cut ties with the past, with [Collins Obuya](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Collins_Obuya "Collins Obuya"), the new captain, being the oldest player at 29. Experienced players like the former captain [Jimmy Kamande](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jimmy_Kamande "Jimmy Kamande"), a veteran of five World Cups, [Thomas Odoyo](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Thomas_Odoyo "Thomas Odoyo"), and others were not even considered. As was expected, the left-out players were quick to retort as Kamande said that "the board was selecting players who would be their puppets", while Odoyo opined that "it was malicious and not done in good faith". According to them, it was fast-tracking the death of Kenyan cricket. They were also supported by the Kenyan media.[[105]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kenya_national_cricket_team#cite_note-espncricinfo.com-106)

Among the 20 cricketers offered contracts, 13 of them were offered central contracts. To complicate things further, five players turned down those contracts: [Alex Obanda](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Alex_Obanda "Alex Obanda"), [Shem Ngoche](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Shem_Ngoche "Shem Ngoche"), [James Ngoche](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/James_Ngoche "James Ngoche"), [Nehemiah Odhiambo](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nehemiah_Odhiambo "Nehemiah Odhiambo"), and [Elijah Otieno](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Elijah_Otieno "Elijah Otieno"). Sears said that they were pleased with the group of seven players who committed to Cricket Kenya, while equally disappointed with those who refused contracts.[[106]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kenya_national_cricket_team#cite_note-107) Accordingly, they were left out of the squad to face the [UAE](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/United_Arab_Emirates_national_cricket_team "United Arab Emirates national cricket team") in the [ICC Intercontinental Cup](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/ICC_Intercontinental_Cup "ICC Intercontinental Cup").[[107]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kenya_national_cricket_team#cite_note-108)

Cricket Kenya offered contracts to more young players, such as opening batsman [Runish Gudhka](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Runish_Gudhka "Runish Gudhka") from [Nairobi](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nairobi "Nairobi"), the Australian-born all-rounder [Duncan Allan](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Duncan_Allan "Duncan Allan"), wicketkeeper [Irfan Karim](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Irfan_Karim "Irfan Karim"), and fast bowlers such as [Emmanuel Ringera](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Emmanuel_Ringera "Emmanuel Ringera"), Ibrahim Akello, and [Dominic Wesonga](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dominic_Wesonga "Dominic Wesonga"), who had performed well in the regional NPCA and East African leagues.[[108]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kenya_national_cricket_team#cite_note-109)

However, the eight players who had refused the contracts offered by the board, with former skipper [Morris Ouma](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Morris_Ouma "Morris Ouma"), [Alfred Luseno](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Alfred_Luseno "Alfred Luseno") and [Nelson Odhiambo](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nelson_Odhiambo "Nelson Odhiambo") being late inclusions, asked their views to be heard, and despite the board granting them another chance, they finally took a firm stance against them. While Obanda, Shem and James Ngoche, Odhiambo, and Otieno were made renewed offers, while Ouma, Luseno, and Nelson had a three-month agreement till March 2012 subject to performance. If they could do something good, they could retain their spot in the team. Sears said of this debacle,"It's a shame that yet again some of these players have turned down their contracts but that is their choice. We met with these players as we promised we would, we listened to their views and made them offers that reflected what they wanted – an agreement that would run until the end of the contract year in May 2012 if they met certain performance criteria which all players have to meet. Perhaps the most disappointing aspect was that they refused to represent their teams in the East African Competitions last weekend pulling out at the very last minute. Again sadly it calls into question the professionalism of these players, how committed they are to putting in the effort, their application in fulfilling their potential and the advice they have been getting from their advisors."[[109]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kenya_national_cricket_team#cite_note-110)

Another reform was to appoint the former [Otago](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Otago_cricket_team "Otago cricket team") coach [Mike Hesson](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mike_Hesson "Mike Hesson") as the national coach.[[110]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kenya_national_cricket_team#cite_note-111) Immediately afterwards, Hesson announced that he was here to resolve and put to end the dispute between the players and the board. He said that in an interview to the newspaper [Otago Daily Times](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Otago_Daily_Times "Otago Daily Times").[[111]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kenya_national_cricket_team#cite_note-112)

The East Africa finals were rescheduled from October to December 2011 due to heavy showers in Nairobi at that time.[[112]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kenya_national_cricket_team#cite_note-113) However, once again, heavy showers in December led the finals again being postponed to January 2012.[[113]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kenya_national_cricket_team#cite_note-114)

### Loss of ODI status: 2014–2023

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Kenya_national_cricket_team&action=edit&section=12 "Edit section: Loss of ODI status: 2014–2023")]

[![Image 28](https://thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/en/thumb/b/b6/Pushkar_Sharma_in_training_session%2C_Nairobi%2C_Kenya%2C_2022.jpeg/250px-Pushkar_Sharma_in_training_session%2C_Nairobi%2C_Kenya%2C_2022.jpeg?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:Pushkar_Sharma_in_training_session,_Nairobi,_Kenya,_2022.jpeg)

[Pushkar Sharma](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pushkar_Sharma_(cricketer) "Pushkar Sharma (cricketer)") made his debut for the national cricket team of Kenya in the 2020s.

Kenya lost their ODI status after 18 years when they finished outside the top 4 in the [2014 Cricket World Cup Qualifier](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2014_Cricket_World_Cup_Qualifier "2014 Cricket World Cup Qualifier") also failing to qualify for the [2015 Cricket World Cup](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2015_Cricket_World_Cup "2015 Cricket World Cup").[[114]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kenya_national_cricket_team#cite_note-115)

Further failures in the [World Cricket League](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/World_Cricket_League "World Cricket League"), including a defeat to the [USA](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/United_States_national_cricket_team "United States national cricket team"), meant that Kenya couldn't regain their ODI status while being subsequently relegated to the new [Challenge League](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cricket_World_Cup_Challenge_League "Cricket World Cup Challenge League").[[115]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kenya_national_cricket_team#cite_note-116)

In April 2018, the ICC decided to grant full [Twenty20 International](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Twenty20_International "Twenty20 International") (T20I) status to all its members. Therefore, all [Twenty20](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Twenty20 "Twenty20") cricket matches played between Kenya and other [ICC members](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_International_Cricket_Council_members "List of International Cricket Council members") since 1 January 2019 have been full T20I matches.[[7]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kenya_national_cricket_team#cite_note-International_Cricket_Council-8)

### Recent developments

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Kenya_national_cricket_team&action=edit&section=13 "Edit section: Recent developments")]

The Kenyan cricket team reached the [final stage of the Africa Qualifier](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2023_Men's_T20_World_Cup_Africa_regional_final "2023 Men's T20 World Cup Africa regional final") for the [2024 Men's T20 World Cup](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2024_Men's_T20_World_Cup "2024 Men's T20 World Cup") but narrowly missed out on qualification. In an effort to strengthen their performance and strategy, Cricket Kenya appointed former Indian cricketer [Dodda Ganesh](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dodda_Ganesh "Dodda Ganesh") as the new head coach, bringing in his extensive experience to guide the team in future competitions.

From October 19 to 24, 2024, Cricket Kenya hosted the [T20 World Cup Africa Sub-Regional Qualifier B](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2024_Men's_T20_World_Cup_Africa_Sub-regional_Qualifier_B "2024 Men's T20 World Cup Africa Sub-regional Qualifier B") in Nairobi.[[116]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kenya_national_cricket_team#cite_note-117) Kenya delivered a strong performance throughout the Sub-Regional Qualifier, securing victories that saw them advance alongside Zimbabwe to the [regional final](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2025_Men's_T20_World_Cup_Africa_Regional_Final "2025 Men's T20 World Cup Africa Regional Final"). The qualification brought them one step closer to securing a place in the [2026 Men's T20 World Cup](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2026_Men's_T20_World_Cup "2026 Men's T20 World Cup"). However, Kenya once again failed to progress from the regional final.
