_As of 3 October 2026_

The **Namibia****men's national cricket team** represents [Namibia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Namibia "Namibia") in [international cricket](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/International_cricket "International cricket"). It is administered by [Cricket Namibia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cricket_Namibia "Cricket Namibia"), the governing body of cricket in Namibia, which has been an [associate member](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_International_Cricket_Council_members "List of International Cricket Council members") of the [International Cricket Council](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/International_Cricket_Council "International Cricket Council") since 1992.

A team representing [South West Africa](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/South_West_Africa "South West Africa") played in South African domestic competitions prior to Namibia's independence in 1990. After joining the ICC, the country soon became one of the leading ICC associate members in Africa. Namibia finished second at the [2001 ICC Trophy](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2001_ICC_Trophy "2001 ICC Trophy"), thereby qualifying for the [2003 Cricket World Cup](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2003_Cricket_World_Cup "2003 Cricket World Cup") in South Africa. The team made its [One Day International](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/One_Day_International "One Day International") (ODI) debut at the tournament but failed to win a match. Beginning in 2004, Namibia participated in every edition of the [ICC Intercontinental Cup](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/ICC_Intercontinental_Cup "ICC Intercontinental Cup"), finishing runners-up [in 2007–08](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2007%E2%80%9308_ICC_Intercontinental_Cup "2007–08 ICC Intercontinental Cup"). It also featured at the highest levels of the [World Cricket League](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/World_Cricket_League "World Cricket League") (WCL), twice participating in the [WCL Championship](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/ICC_World_Cricket_League_Championship "ICC World Cricket League Championship"), and finished third at the [2012 ICC World Twenty20 Qualifier](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2012_ICC_World_Twenty20_Qualifier "2012 ICC World Twenty20 Qualifier").

Namibia were runners-up at the [2019 WCL Division Two](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2019_ICC_World_Cricket_League_Division_Two "2019 ICC World Cricket League Division Two") tournament to secure the [ODI](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/One_Day_International "One Day International") status and qualify for the [2019–2023 ICC Cricket World Cup League 2](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2019%E2%80%932023_ICC_Cricket_World_Cup_League_2 "2019–2023 ICC Cricket World Cup League 2"). The team finished fourth at the [2019 ICC Men's T20 World Cup Qualifier](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2019_ICC_Men's_T20_World_Cup_Qualifier "2019 ICC Men's T20 World Cup Qualifier") to qualify for the [2021 ICC Men's T20 World Cup](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2021_ICC_Men's_T20_World_Cup "2021 ICC Men's T20 World Cup"). It subsequently recorded its first World Cup victories, defeating the [Netherlands](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Netherlands_national_cricket_team "Netherlands national cricket team") and [Ireland](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ireland_national_cricket_team "Ireland national cricket team") in the first round of the tournament to progress to the Super 12 stage.

## History

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Namibia_national_cricket_team&action=edit&section=1 "Edit section: History")]

The earliest instance of cricket being played in [Windhoek](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Windhoek "Windhoek") dates back to 1909 when [South West Africa](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/South_West_Africa "South West Africa") was very much a German colony.[[6]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Namibia_national_cricket_team#cite_note-7) During the [First World War](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/First_World_War "First World War") (1914), South African troops opened assault in the region. A game of cricket was recorded in the Okonjande prisoner of war camp near Otjiwarongo.[[7]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Namibia_national_cricket_team#cite_note-8) South Africa captured [South West Africa](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/South_West_Africa "South West Africa") following Germany's defeat. It came under the [League of Nations](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/League_of_Nations_mandate "League of Nations mandate") mandate in the [Union of South Africa](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Union_of_South_Africa "Union of South Africa").

Following this, cricket was regularly played in the Western Province. The South West Africa Cricket Union was formed in 1930 and the first organised matches were played in the region.[[8]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Namibia_national_cricket_team#cite_note-9)[South West Africa](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/South_West_Africa "South West Africa") began playing in the South African Country Cricket Association's annual competition in the 1961–62 season.[[9]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Namibia_national_cricket_team#cite_note-SA-10)

### South West Africa (1961–1989)

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Namibia_national_cricket_team&action=edit&section=2 "Edit section: South West Africa (1961–1989)")]

[South West Africa](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/South_West_Africa "South West Africa") competed in the South African Country Cricket Association's annual competition between 1961 and 1989.[[9]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Namibia_national_cricket_team#cite_note-SA-10) In 1966, the [Namibian war of Independence](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/South_African_Border_War "South African Border War") was launched by the [People's Liberation Army of Namibia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/People's_Liberation_Army_of_Namibia "People's Liberation Army of Namibia"), an armed wing of [SWAPO](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/SWAPO "SWAPO"). South West African rebels welcomed the sporting boycott of the South African apartheid regime and lent their support to the "Stop the seventy tour" campaign.

South West Africa played their last domestic season in South Africa in January 1989. In April, [PLAN](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/People's_Liberation_Army_of_Namibia "People's Liberation Army of Namibia") launched its [final guerrilla campaign](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Operation_Merlyn "Operation Merlyn") and the South West Africa Cricket Union severed their ties with the South African Cricket Board (SACB).

In November 1989, a Namibian team toured Botswana and played their first international fixture,[[10]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Namibia_national_cricket_team#cite_note-11) although the [Namibian Cricket Board](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cricket_Namibia "Cricket Namibia") were not affiliated to the [International Cricket Council](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/International_Cricket_Council "International Cricket Council") until 1992.[[11]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Namibia_national_cricket_team#cite_note-NamCA-12)

### Initial years

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Namibia_national_cricket_team&action=edit&section=3 "Edit section: Initial years")]

After the Botswana tour, [Gloucestershire County Cricket Club](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gloucestershire_County_Cricket_Club "Gloucestershire County Cricket Club") visited Namibia in March 1990, taking part in the Independence Day celebrations.[[12]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Namibia_national_cricket_team#cite_note-13) This was followed by a visit from [The Netherlands](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Netherlands_national_cricket_team "Netherlands national cricket team") in April.[[13]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Namibia_national_cricket_team#cite_note-14) Before the formation of the [African Cricket Association](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/African_Cricket_Association "African Cricket Association"), the SCSA Zone VI cricket federation was formed after two schoolboy cricket tours between Namibia and Botswana in 1989 and 1990.[[14]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Namibia_national_cricket_team#cite_note-audiodata.cricinfo.com-15) The inaugural ACA tournament was held in Windhoek in September 1991, with Zambia, Malawi, Namibia, Lesotho and Botswana playing as well as an [Oxford University Cricket Club](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Oxford_University_Cricket_Club "Oxford University Cricket Club") side.[[14]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Namibia_national_cricket_team#cite_note-audiodata.cricinfo.com-15)

### 2003 World Cup

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Namibia_national_cricket_team&action=edit&section=4 "Edit section: 2003 World Cup")]

The road to the [2003 Cricket World Cup](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2003_Cricket_World_Cup "2003 Cricket World Cup") started with the [2001 ICC Trophy](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2001_ICC_Trophy "2001 ICC Trophy") in Canada. Namibia reached the final at the [Toronto Cricket, Skating and Curling Club](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Toronto_Cricket,_Skating_and_Curling_Club "Toronto Cricket, Skating and Curling Club"), losing to the Netherlands, but still qualifying for their first World Cup.[[15]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Namibia_national_cricket_team#cite_note-ICCT01-16) Namibia then hosted the [ICC 6 Nations Challenge](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/ICC_6_Nations_Challenge "ICC 6 Nations Challenge") in April 2002, finishing fourth[[16]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Namibia_national_cricket_team#cite_note-ICC6N02-17) and had a disappointing Africa Cup campaign that September, finishing fourth in their group and beating only [Tanzania](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tanzania_national_cricket_team "Tanzania national cricket team"),[[17]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Namibia_national_cricket_team#cite_note-18) before losing four matches against Zimbabwe A a few weeks later.[[18]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Namibia_national_cricket_team#cite_note-19) A tour of Kenya was more successful, as Namibia beat [Kenya](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kenya_national_cricket_team "Kenya national cricket team") in a four match one-day series.[[19]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Namibia_national_cricket_team#cite_note-20) Following this, Namibia took part in the top level of South African domestic one-day cricket, the Standard Bank Cup, but lost all five of their games.[[20]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Namibia_national_cricket_team#cite_note-21) Bangladesh toured in January 2003, winning the five match one-day series 4–1.[[21]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Namibia_national_cricket_team#cite_note-22)

The World Cup itself started on 10 February 2003 in [Harare](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Harare "Harare") with [Zimbabwe](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Zimbabwe_national_cricket_team "Zimbabwe national cricket team") beating Namibia by 86 runs in Namibia's debut [One Day International](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/One_Day_International "One Day International") (ODI).[[22]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Namibia_national_cricket_team#cite_note-23)

### After the World Cup

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Namibia_national_cricket_team&action=edit&section=5 "Edit section: After the World Cup")]

In August 2003, Zimbabwe A toured Namibia. Namibia won the one-day series 2–1, but lost both three-day games.[[30]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Namibia_national_cricket_team#cite_note-31) A return visit to Zimbabwe the following January saw Namibia win a five match one-day series against Zimbabwe A 4–1, also winning a match against Zimbabwe Under-19s.[[31]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Namibia_national_cricket_team#cite_note-32) Bangladesh toured Namibia in February, winning all three one-day games and drawing the three-day game.[[32]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Namibia_national_cricket_team#cite_note-33) Following this, Namibia travelled to the United Arab Emirates for the [2004 ICC Six Nations Challenge](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2004_ICC_Six_Nations_Challenge "2004 ICC Six Nations Challenge"). They finished third on run rate after beating [Canada](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Canada_national_cricket_team "Canada national cricket team"), the Netherlands and the [UAE](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/United_Arab_Emirates_national_cricket_team "United Arab Emirates national cricket team") and losing to Scotland and the [USA](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/United_States_national_cricket_team "United States national cricket team").[[33]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Namibia_national_cricket_team#cite_note-ICC6N04-34) Namibia played two [ICC Intercontinental Cup](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/ICC_Intercontinental_Cup "ICC Intercontinental Cup") matches against Kenya and [Uganda](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Uganda_national_cricket_team "Uganda national cricket team") in 2004, losing them both.[[34]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Namibia_national_cricket_team#cite_note-ICCup04-35) In between the two matches, they won an African nations tournament in Zambia.[[35]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Namibia_national_cricket_team#cite_note-36) Later in the year, they took part in Zimbabwe's national one-day domestic competition, in which they finished as runners-up.[[36]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Namibia_national_cricket_team#cite_note-37) Whilst in Zimbabwe, they won two matches against the national side.[[37]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Namibia_national_cricket_team#cite_note-38) This was followed by a visit to Namibia by England, who won both matches.[[38]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Namibia_national_cricket_team#cite_note-39)

Zimbabwe A again visited Namibia in early 2005, losing both one-day matches that finished.[[39]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Namibia_national_cricket_team#cite_note-40) Pakistan A were the next visitors in April, winning all three one-day matches and drawing in the three-day game.[[40]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Namibia_national_cricket_team#cite_note-41) This was followed by their two regional group games in the [2005 ICC Intercontinental Cup](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2005_ICC_Intercontinental_Cup "2005 ICC Intercontinental Cup"). Whilst they were unbeaten, winning against Uganda and drawing against Kenya, this was not enough to qualify for the semi-finals.[[41]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Namibia_national_cricket_team#cite_note-ICCup05-42) They then visited Ireland to take part in the [2005 ICC Trophy](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2005_ICC_Trophy "2005 ICC Trophy"). They finished 7th after beating Denmark in their final play-off game.[[42]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Namibia_national_cricket_team#cite_note-ICCT05-43) Back at home, they hosted [New Zealand](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/New_Zealand_national_cricket_team "New Zealand national cricket team") at the end of July, losing both games,[[43]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Namibia_national_cricket_team#cite_note-44) losing by only 29 runs after conceding 330/6.[[44]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Namibia_national_cricket_team#cite_note-45) In October of that year, they hosted the semi-finals of the Intercontinental Cup, despite failing to qualify. While the final was being played, they played a two match one-day series against Bermuda after they had been knocked out of the tournament, winning both games, but the games were tarnished by controversial incidents, with the Bermuda team accusing the Namibian team of racist insults, and walking off in the second game when a flurry of [bouncers](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bouncer_(cricket) "Bouncer (cricket)") were unleashed at the lower order Bermuda batsmen.[[45]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Namibia_national_cricket_team#cite_note-46) The Namibian Cricket Board denied the allegations of racism.[[46]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Namibia_national_cricket_team#cite_note-47)

In March 2006, Namibia met [Nepal](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nepal_national_cricket_team "Nepal national cricket team") in a challenge match to decide who got the eighth and final spot in the [2006 ICC Intercontinental Cup](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2006_ICC_Intercontinental_Cup "2006 ICC Intercontinental Cup"). The match was drawn, with Namibia getting a first innings lead, thus qualifying them for the main tournament. The main tournament itself started with an innings defeat by Scotland in [Aberdeen](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Aberdeen "Aberdeen") before a five wicket defeat by [Ireland](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ireland_cricket_team "Ireland cricket team") in Dublin, both matches in May.[[47]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Namibia_national_cricket_team#cite_note-ICCup06-48) In the [2006–07 South African cricket season](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2006%E2%80%9307_South_African_cricket_season "2006–07 South African cricket season"), Namibia took part in the second tier of [first-class](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/First-class_cricket "First-class cricket") and [List A cricket](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_A_cricket "List A cricket"), the South African Airways Challenge. They finished second in their group in the three-day tournament[[48]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Namibia_national_cricket_team#cite_note-49) and third in their group in the one-day tournament, missing out on reaching the semi-finals by one win.[[49]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Namibia_national_cricket_team#cite_note-50) In the midst of the matches in those tournaments, they played their third and final 2006 Intercontinental Cup match, beating the UAE by an innings.[[47]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Namibia_national_cricket_team#cite_note-ICCup06-48) On 1 April 2007, they became part of the ICC's High Performance Program.[[50]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Namibia_national_cricket_team#cite_note-HPP-51)

In November/December 2007, Namibia hosted [Division Two](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2007_ICC_World_Cricket_League_Division_Two "2007 ICC World Cricket League Division Two") of the [World Cricket League](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/World_Cricket_League "World Cricket League") where they played against [Argentina](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Argentina_national_cricket_team "Argentina national cricket team"), [Denmark](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Danish_cricket_team "Danish cricket team"), [Oman](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Oman_national_cricket_team "Oman national cricket team"), [the UAE](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/United_Arab_Emirates_cricket_team "United Arab Emirates cricket team") and [Uganda](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ugandan_cricket_team "Ugandan cricket team"). Although Namibia won three of their five group matches, it was not enough for them to progress to the final. Namibia beat Denmark in the third place playoff. On the basis of their top four finish in this tournament, Namibia qualified for the [ICC World Cup Qualifier](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/ICC_World_Cup_Qualifier "ICC World Cup Qualifier") in 2009, the final tournament in qualification for the [2011 World Cup](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2011_Cricket_World_Cup "2011 Cricket World Cup").

Namibia again took part in the second tier of South African domestic cricket between October 2007 and February 2008.[[51]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Namibia_national_cricket_team#cite_note-52) They played a [2007–08 ICC Intercontinental Cup](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2007%E2%80%9308_ICC_Intercontinental_Cup "2007–08 ICC Intercontinental Cup") match against Canada in October 2007, playing the remaining games against Bermuda, Ireland, Kenya, the Netherlands, Scotland and the UAE in 2008.[[52]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Namibia_national_cricket_team#cite_note-ICCup08-53)

Namibia won the [2009–10 ICC Intercontinental Shield](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2009%E2%80%9310_ICC_Intercontinental_Shield "2009–10 ICC Intercontinental Shield") defeating the [United Arab Emirates](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/United_Arab_Emirates_national_cricket_team "United Arab Emirates national cricket team") by six wickets in Dubai.[[53]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Namibia_national_cricket_team#cite_note-54) In 2011 Namibia participated in [Division Two](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2011_ICC_World_Cricket_League_Division_Two "2011 ICC World Cricket League Division Two") and finished as runners-up, on this occasion behind the UAE.[[54]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Namibia_national_cricket_team#cite_note-55)

In July 2011, the country competed in the ICC Twenty20 World Cricket League Africa Division One competition in Uganda, winning all eight group matches before succumbing to the [hosts](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Uganda_national_cricket_team "Uganda national cricket team") in the Final by six wickets.[[55]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Namibia_national_cricket_team#cite_note-56) During this tournament, all-rounder Louis van der Westhuizen struck 16 sixes in an innings of 159* against Kenya, as part of a team total of 262/1 from 20 overs.

### The Golden Generation

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Namibia_national_cricket_team&action=edit&section=6 "Edit section: The Golden Generation")]

In April 2018, the ICC decided to grant full [Twenty20 International](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Twenty20_International "Twenty20 International") (T20I) status to all its members. Therefore, all [Twenty20](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Twenty20 "Twenty20") matches played between Namibia and other [ICC members](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_International_Cricket_Council_members "List of International Cricket Council members") since 1 January 2019 have the full T20I status.[[56]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Namibia_national_cricket_team#cite_note-57) Namibia's first T20I match was against [Ghana](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ghana_national_cricket_team "Ghana national cricket team") on 20 May 2019 in the Regional Final of the [2018–19 ICC World Twenty20 Africa Qualifier](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2018%E2%80%9319_ICC_World_Twenty20_Africa_Qualifier "2018–19 ICC World Twenty20 Africa Qualifier") tournament. They won the match comfortably.

In July 2020, the Namibia Men's team won the ICC Associate Member Men's Performance of the Year award, after gaining [One Day International](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/One_Day_International "One Day International") (ODI) status, in the ICC's Annual Development Awards to recognise developing cricketing nations.[[57]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Namibia_national_cricket_team#cite_note-58)[[58]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Namibia_national_cricket_team#cite_note-59)

Namibia qualified for the [2021 ICC T20 World Cup](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2021_ICC_T20_World_Cup "2021 ICC T20 World Cup") in the [United Arab Emirates](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/United_Arab_Emirates "United Arab Emirates") when they finished 4th in the [2019 ICC Men's T20 World Cup Qualifier](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2019_ICC_Men's_T20_World_Cup_Qualifier "2019 ICC Men's T20 World Cup Qualifier") tournament in October and November 2019.[[59]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Namibia_national_cricket_team#cite_note-NAM-60) They lost their first match against Sri Lanka but recorded a historic first-ever win at a World Cup event when they beat The Netherlands by 6 wickets in Abu Dhabi on 20 October 2021.[[60]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Namibia_national_cricket_team#cite_note-61) On 22 October 2021 in the next match against Ireland, Namibia made history by winning the match by 8 wickets and qualified for the Super 12 stage of the tournament.[[61]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Namibia_national_cricket_team#cite_note-62)[[62]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Namibia_national_cricket_team#cite_note-63) On 27 October 2021, in the first Super 12 match for Namibia, they registered another historic win, defeating Scotland by 4 wickets.

Namibia are participating in the inaugural [2023 Cricket World Cup Qualifier Play-off](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2023_Cricket_World_Cup_Qualifier_Play-off "2023 Cricket World Cup Qualifier Play-off"), a part of the qualification process for [2023 Cricket World Cup](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2023_Cricket_World_Cup "2023 Cricket World Cup"), as the hosts.[[63]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Namibia_national_cricket_team#cite_note-64) They got their maiden win in the tournament against [Papua New Guinea](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Papua_New_Guinea_national_cricket_team "Papua New Guinea national cricket team"), as they won the match by 48 runs.[[64]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Namibia_national_cricket_team#cite_note-65) Namibia's score of 381/8 was the highest total by an [associate nation](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_International_Cricket_Council_members#Associate_Members "List of International Cricket Council members") in an ODI match.[[65]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Namibia_national_cricket_team#cite_note-66)

The [South African cricket team](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/South_Africa_national_cricket_team "South Africa national cricket team") toured Namibia in October 2025 for a one-off [Twenty20 International](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Twenty20_International "Twenty20 International") (T20I) match to inaugurate the opening of Cricket Namibia's first official stadium, the [Namibia Cricket Ground](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Namibia_Cricket_Ground "Namibia Cricket Ground") in [Windhoek](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Windhoek "Windhoek").[[66]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Namibia_national_cricket_team#cite_note-67)[[67]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Namibia_national_cricket_team#cite_note-68) It was the first-ever international match between the two sides.[[68]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Namibia_national_cricket_team#cite_note-69) Namibia won the match by 4 wickets in a last ball thrilling upset.[[69]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Namibia_national_cricket_team#cite_note-70)[[70]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Namibia_national_cricket_team#cite_note-71)

Additionally, the Man of the Match award was given to a player who scored over 65 runs and remained not out.

# Rakep Patel leads Kenya to 42-run win

15 July, 2015

[](https://www.facebook.com/sharer/sharer.php?u=https%3A%2F%2Fwww.icc-cricket.com%2Fnews%2Frakep-patel-leads-kenya-to-42-run-win)[](https://twitter.com/intent/tweet?url=https%3A%2F%2Fwww.icc-cricket.com%2Fnews%2Frakep-patel-leads-kenya-to-42-run-win&text=Rakep%20Patel%20leads%20Kenya%20to%2042-run%20win)

![Image 18: 69292 ](link_35)

![Image 19: 69292 ](link_36)

An impressive batting performance helped Kenya beat the United Arab Emirates by 42 runs in Edinburgh on Wednesday (July 15) to join Afghanistan at the top of the Group B standings.

Rakep Patel, the captain, led from the front with a 27-ball 50 in Kenya's 147 for 5 in 20 overs. Once UAE's chase went awry in the first six overs, there was little the middle order could do to salvage the match as it was bowled out for 105 in 17.2 overs to slip to its fourth loss in five matches.

There was hope at the start though as Mohammad Naved, the medium pacer, struck twice to reduce Kenya to 36 for 2 at the end of the Power Play overs. But Narendra Patel ensured Kenya didn't slip into damage control mode as he hit boundaries at will in his 29-ball 42.

Collins Obuya, the allrounder, held the innings together in the middle overs with a lively 38-ball 37, but the trigger for the final onslaught came from Rakep. The captain stroked three fours and as many sixes in his half-century before being dismissed off the final ball courtesy Nasir Aziz's direct hit to give Kenya momentum going into the break.

Rakep was pleased with the way his side stepped up and said he would continue to bat aggressive in the rest of the matches. "It was a do or die for us to stay in the competition and we just believed in each other," he said. "I had to bat aggressively to take the team through and I'm looking do that in every innings."

Only two of UAE's top five crossed 20 in a chase that needed at least one batsman to bat right through. Faizan Asif made a solid 21, but it wasn’t until Shaiman Anwar's arrival that UAE started to push. Anwar, who came in at No. 5, top scored with a 15-ball 25.

But the top order collapse meant UAE's challenge fizzled out. The last five wickets fell for just 28 runs with Narendra Patel picking up four wickets to walk away with top honours in an impressive victory.

“The way the wicket was playing I thought we got quite a good score and we could defend it with the bowling attack we have," said Narendra.

With three wins in five matches, only net run-rate separated Kenya from table topper Afghanistan, who was pipped earlier in the day by Oman.

# France stun Belgium with four late goals to snatch victory

![Image 4](https://espnmedia-cdn.akamaized.net/espn/media/common/2026/1005/dm_261005_COM_SOC_ANALYSIS_Leboeuf_Olise_and_France_looked_unstoppable_2026_5_10/dm_261005_COM_SOC_ANALYSIS_Leboeuf_Olise_and_France_looked_unstoppable_2026_5_10.jpg)

## Leboeuf: Olise and France looked unstoppable

* * *

By PA

Oct 5, 2026, 08:57 pm

Facebook Facebook Messenger Twitter Email

Zinedine Zidane's [France](http://espn.com/soccer/team?id=478) belatedly turned on the style as late goals from substitutes [Désiré Doué](http://espn.com/soccer/player/_/id/336388/desire-doue), Ryan Cherki and two from [Michael Olise](http://espn.com/soccer/player/_/id/286831/michael-olise) saw them come from behind to beat [Belgium](http://espn.com/soccer/team?id=459) 4-1 in the [UEFA Nations League](https://www.espn.com/soccer/league/_/name/UEFA.NATIONS).

France cemented their place at the top of Group A after battling to a first home win under new boss Zidane.

[Dodi Lukébakio](http://espn.com/soccer/player/_/id/229443/dodi-lukebakio) had fired Belgium into a first-half lead which they held on to until the 77th minute at the Stade de France.

But Zidane's substitutions paid dividends with four goals in the last 13 minutes leaving France on 10 points after four games.

Recalled [Romelu Lukaku](http://espn.com/soccer/player/_/id/139437/romelu-lukaku) had an early chance for the visitors when he spun away from his marker, but his shot was gathered by [Toulouse](http://espn.com/soccer/team?id=179) goalkeeper [Guillaume Restes](http://espn.com/soccer/player/_/id/324289/guillaume-restes) on his debut.

[Nicolas Raskin](http://espn.com/soccer/player/_/id/260027/nicolas-raskin) then headed Lukebakio's cross narrowly over with France living dangerously.

The hosts were adamant they should have had a penalty when the ball struck the arm of [Nathan Ngoy](http://espn.com/soccer/player/_/id/318577/nathan-ngoy) in the box but their claims were turned down.

France should have gone ahead in the 33rd minute when [Ousmane Dembélé](http://espn.com/soccer/player/_/id/229744/ousmane-dembele) raced down the right and squared the ball for [Esteban Lepaul](http://espn.com/soccer/player/_/id/323850/esteban-lepaul), who lifted his shot over from 14 yards.

Barely a minute later they fell behind after Lukebakio beat the offside trap to race on to Romeo Lavia's long ball out from the back.

The [Benfica](http://espn.com/soccer/team?id=1929) winger held his nerve to slot a superb finish past Restes and high into the net.

France pushed for an equaliser after the break and Manu Kone's effort was blocked by the shoulder of Lavia, before Dembele curled a short inches wide of the far post.

Zidane had seen enough by the hour mark and sent on Cherki and Olise. Cherki immediately fed his fellow substitute but the [Bayern Munich](http://espn.com/soccer/team?id=132) star's shot was straight at [Maarten Vandevoordt](http://espn.com/soccer/player/_/id/277377/maarten-vandevoordt).

Belgium keeper Vandevoordt then marked his debut with a superb finger-tip save to keep out Cherki's curling effort, before Bradley Barcola's shot was deflected wide.

But it was the third substitute, Doue, who grabbed the equaliser when he received the ball with his back to goal on the edge of the box, turned and arrowed a low shot into the far corner.

Three minute later Olise darted to the byline and pulled the ball back for Cherki to crash home. With two minutes left Olise held off Raskin before firing across Vandevoordt and into the net.

Doue then slipped in Olise for number four in stoppage time to cap a remarkable denouement in Paris.

The game of cricket

The Nigerian national cricket team‘s quest to win the ICC World T20 Africa Qualifier ‘A’ continued yesterday when the side recorded a convincing 55 runs victory over The Gambian at the Tafawa Balewa Cricket Oval in Lagos.
Captain Chimezie Onwuzulike’s decision to bat first after winning the toss paid off as Nigeria posted 176 runs for loss of five wickets in 20 overs. Basiru Jaye was the best bowler for the fielding side with two wickets, 16 runs in three overs.

Vice Captain, Ademola Onikoyi, top scored with 74 runs not out off 39 balls with nine fours and two sixes. Chimezie Onwuzulike added 34 runs, Isaac Okpe put in 21 runs not out with lovely three sixes and Opening batsman, Sulaimon Runsewe dropped 18 runs.  
  
 The Nigerian bowlers in the second innings ensured the mountain was too high for Captain Mbye Dumbuya’s team to climb as The Gambia was reduced to 121 runs for seven wickets in 20 overs.

Debutant Daniel Gim claimed two wickets for 16 runs in three overs, while the quartet of Isaac Danladi, Shola Anyia, Seye Olympio and Isaac Okpe all had a wicket each.

Advertisement

Pa Assan Faye led the batting onslaught for his side with 29 runs off 16 balls, Mohammed Manga 24 runs and Andrew Jarju contributed 15 runs.

This victory (Nigeria has won two matches, including the opening victory against Sierra Leone and the defeat of The Gambia) means that qualification for the next stage of the qualifiers is in sight.

The big decider of which team will top the qualifier will come on Tuesday when Nigeria clashes with bitter rivals, Ghana at the same venue.

# Italian renaissance continues with runaway win over Türkiye

By PA

Updated: Oct 5, 2026, 09:24 pm

Facebook Facebook Messenger Twitter Email

Pio Esposito's late goal sealed a hard-earned win over [Türkiye](link_13) in [Bologna](link_14) and continued Italy's improvement under returning head coach Roberto Mancini.

The hosts survived some tough moments to secure a 3-1 win and a quickfire double over their opponents, boosting their chances of a place in the Nations League quarterfinals.

Mancini's men went into the game after a creditable draw with [France](link_15) and a thumping 4-1 win over the Turks in Bursa last month, but they found the going tougher on home turf.

[Italy](link_16) started well against their opponents, who went into the game still searching for their point in the group, and [Gianluca Scamacca](link_17) fired the first chance just wide of target in the 11th minute.

Irfan Kahveci served a timely reminder that his side were intent on breaking their duck when he burst onto a clever through-ball moments later, but lost control when he could have been clean through on keeper [Gianluigi Donnarumma](link_18).

Türkiye kept coming forward, and [Ozan Kabak](link_19) was next to come close to breaking the deadlock when his shot from the edge of the box was pushed out for a corner by Donnarumma.

![Image 6: Italy players celebrate after scoring a goal against Turkiye in the Nations League.](https://a.espncdn.com/photo/2026/1005/r1726523_1296x729_16-9.jpg)

Italy players celebrate after scoring a goal against Turkiye in the Nations League.

Getty Images

* * *

The veteran keeper also saved well from [Salih Özcan](link_20) before Italy snatched their first real opportunity to go in front four minutes before the half-hour mark.

[Antonio Vergara](link_21) and Giovanni De Lorenzo combined well before Vergara fired a cross that took a deflection and fell nicely for Scamacca to ram it home off the underside of the bar.

Italy looked more settled having made their breakthrough and sat comfortably on their lead until just before the hour mark, when [Issa Doumbia](link_22) was denied his side's second by a strong save from Türkiye keeper [Ugurcan Çakir](link_23).

Türkiye grabbed their chance to score a shock equaliser four minutes later when the ball flicked off [Eren Elmali](link_24) into the path of [Aral Simsir](link_25), who had the simplest of chances to poke home from point-blank range.

Mancini's men regrouped and regained their lead within four minutes after [Nicolò Barella](link_26) delivered a free kick from the right that was met by the rising [Riccardo Calafiori](link_27) who headed past Cakir.

Donnarumma did well to preserve Italy's hard-earned advantage in the 77th minute when he tipped away a drive from Ozcan, who had been played through by a pinpoint cross from [Yunus Akgün](link_28).

Esposito finally wrapped up the win in the 88th minute after Doumbia drove brilliantly into the box, his shot bouncing clear then being fed back in by Romano for the Inter man to pounce and steer home.

# France stun Belgium with four late goals to snatch victory

![Image 6](https://espnmedia-cdn.akamaized.net/espn/media/common/2026/1005/dm_261005_COM_SOC_ANALYSIS_Leboeuf_Olise_and_France_looked_unstoppable_2026_5_10/dm_261005_COM_SOC_ANALYSIS_Leboeuf_Olise_and_France_looked_unstoppable_2026_5_10.jpg)

## Leboeuf: Olise and France looked unstoppable

* * *

By PA

Oct 5, 2026, 08:57 pm

Facebook Facebook Messenger Twitter Email

Zinedine Zidane's [France](link_14) belatedly turned on the style as late goals from substitutes [Désiré Doué](link_15), Ryan Cherki and two from [Michael Olise](link_16) saw them come from behind to beat [Belgium](link_17) 4-1 in the [UEFA Nations League](link_18).

France cemented their place at the top of Group A after battling to a first home win under new boss Zidane.

[Dodi Lukébakio](link_19) had fired Belgium into a first-half lead which they held on to until the 77th minute at the Stade de France.

But Zidane's substitutions paid dividends with four goals in the last 13 minutes leaving France on 10 points after four games.

Recalled [Romelu Lukaku](link_20) had an early chance for the visitors when he spun away from his marker, but his shot was gathered by [Toulouse](link_21) goalkeeper [Guillaume Restes](link_22) on his debut.

[Nicolas Raskin](link_23) then headed Lukebakio's cross narrowly over with France living dangerously.

The hosts were adamant they should have had a penalty when the ball struck the arm of [Nathan Ngoy](link_24) in the box but their claims were turned down.

France should have gone ahead in the 33rd minute when [Ousmane Dembélé](link_25) raced down the right and squared the ball for [Esteban Lepaul](link_26), who lifted his shot over from 14 yards.

Barely a minute later they fell behind after Lukebakio beat the offside trap to race on to Romeo Lavia's long ball out from the back.

The [Benfica](link_27) winger held his nerve to slot a superb finish past Restes and high into the net.

France pushed for an equaliser after the break and Manu Kone's effort was blocked by the shoulder of Lavia, before Dembele curled a short inches wide of the far post.

Zidane had seen enough by the hour mark and sent on Cherki and Olise. Cherki immediately fed his fellow substitute but the [Bayern Munich](link_28) star's shot was straight at [Maarten Vandevoordt](link_29).

Belgium keeper Vandevoordt then marked his debut with a superb finger-tip save to keep out Cherki's curling effort, before Bradley Barcola's shot was deflected wide.

But it was the third substitute, Doue, who grabbed the equaliser when he received the ball with his back to goal on the edge of the box, turned and arrowed a low shot into the far corner.

Three minute later Olise darted to the byline and pulled the ball back for Cherki to crash home. With two minutes left Olise held off Raskin before firing across Vandevoordt and into the net.

Doue then slipped in Olise for number four in stoppage time to cap a remarkable denouement in Paris.

# Italian renaissance continues with runaway win over Türkiye

By PA

Updated: Oct 5, 2026, 09:24 pm

Facebook Facebook Messenger Twitter Email

Pio Esposito's late goal sealed a hard-earned win over [Türkiye](http://espn.com/soccer/team?id=465) in [Bologna](http://espn.com/soccer/team?id=107) and continued Italy's improvement under returning head coach Roberto Mancini.

The hosts survived some tough moments to secure a 3-1 win and a quickfire double over their opponents, boosting their chances of a place in the Nations League quarterfinals.

Mancini's men went into the game after a creditable draw with [France](http://espn.com/soccer/team?id=478) and a thumping 4-1 win over the Turks in Bursa last month, but they found the going tougher on home turf.

[Italy](http://espn.com/soccer/team?id=162) started well against their opponents, who went into the game still searching for their point in the group, and [Gianluca Scamacca](http://espn.com/soccer/player/_/id/233140/gianluca-scamacca) fired the first chance just wide of target in the 11th minute.

Irfan Kahveci served a timely reminder that his side were intent on breaking their duck when he burst onto a clever through-ball moments later, but lost control when he could have been clean through on keeper [Gianluigi Donnarumma](http://espn.com/soccer/player/_/id/217092/gianluigi-donnarumma).

Türkiye kept coming forward, and [Ozan Kabak](http://espn.com/soccer/player/_/id/266565/ozan-kabak) was next to come close to breaking the deadlock when his shot from the edge of the box was pushed out for a corner by Donnarumma.

![Image 4: Italy players celebrate after scoring a goal against Turkiye in the Nations League.](https://a.espncdn.com/photo/2026/1005/r1726523_1296x729_16-9.jpg)

Italy players celebrate after scoring a goal against Turkiye in the Nations League.

Getty Images

* * *

The veteran keeper also saved well from [Salih Özcan](http://espn.com/soccer/player/_/id/225563/salih-ozcan) before Italy snatched their first real opportunity to go in front four minutes before the half-hour mark.

[Antonio Vergara](http://espn.com/soccer/player/_/id/332411/antonio-vergara) and Giovanni De Lorenzo combined well before Vergara fired a cross that took a deflection and fell nicely for Scamacca to ram it home off the underside of the bar.

Italy looked more settled having made their breakthrough and sat comfortably on their lead until just before the hour mark, when [Issa Doumbia](http://espn.com/soccer/player/_/id/386592/issa-doumbia) was denied his side's second by a strong save from Türkiye keeper [Ugurcan Çakir](http://espn.com/soccer/player/_/id/222922/ugurcan-cakir).

Türkiye grabbed their chance to score a shock equaliser four minutes later when the ball flicked off [Eren Elmali](http://espn.com/soccer/player/_/id/287678/eren-elmali) into the path of [Aral Simsir](http://espn.com/soccer/player/_/id/303000/aral-simsir), who had the simplest of chances to poke home from point-blank range.

Mancini's men regrouped and regained their lead within four minutes after [Nicolò Barella](http://espn.com/soccer/player/_/id/204441/nicolo-barella) delivered a free kick from the right that was met by the rising [Riccardo Calafiori](http://espn.com/soccer/player/_/id/298329/riccardo-calafiori) who headed past Cakir.

Donnarumma did well to preserve Italy's hard-earned advantage in the 77th minute when he tipped away a drive from Ozcan, who had been played through by a pinpoint cross from [Yunus Akgün](http://espn.com/soccer/player/_/id/266575/yunus-akgun).

Esposito finally wrapped up the win in the 88th minute after Doumbia drove brilliantly into the box, his shot bouncing clear then being fed back in by Romano for the Inter man to pounce and steer home.

# AFCON final marred by controversy but Senegal claim title

![Image 4](https://media.video-cdn.espn.com/motion/2026/0119/dm_260119_COM_SOC_INTERVIEW_Morocco_fans_split_after_Brahim_Diazs_penalty_miss_2026_1_19/dm_260119_COM_SOC_INTERVIEW_Morocco_fans_split_after_Brahim_Diazs_penalty_miss_2026_1_19.jpg)

## Morocco fans split after Brahim Diaz's penalty miss

* * *

By Ed Dove

Updated: Jan 18, 2026, 10:29 pm

Facebook Facebook Messenger Twitter Email

![Image 5: Senegal and Morocco players argue during the AFCON final in Rabat.](https://a.espncdn.com/photo/2026/0118/r1602408_1296x729_16-9.jpg)

Senegal and Morocco players argue during the AFCON final in Rabat.

Getty Images

* * *

RABAT, [Morocco](http://espn.com/soccer/team?id=2869) -- An astonishing, emotional AFCON final between [Senegal](http://espn.com/soccer/team?id=654) and Morocco was marred by controversy and supporter violence on Sunday, as [Pape Gueye](http://espn.com/soccer/player/_/id/255889/pape-gueye) fired Senegal to the title in extra time.

Gueye struck the winner after Morocco's [Brahim Díaz](http://espn.com/soccer/player/_/id/246532/brahim-diaz) had missed a penalty in the 20th minute of second-half stoppage time as Senegal won 1-0.

The match was overshadowed by violent altercations between Senegal supporters and Moroccan authorities, as well as both teams, after a VAR decision in stoppage time.

Triumph guaranteed Senegal their second AFCON title following success in 2022 against [Egypt](http://espn.com/soccer/team?id=2620), while a tournament that had promised to be the end of Morocco's 50-year wait for a Nations Cup title ultimately ends in bitter disappointment amidst shocking scenes at the Prince Moulay Abdellah Stadium in Rabat.

The contest descended into controversy and violence in second-half injury time after a pair of refereeing decisions that ruled out a Senegal goal at one end and then awarded a Morocco penalty at the other following a VAR assessment.

Referee Jean-Jacques Ndala's second VAR ruling led to a melee between the two sets of technical teams and players, which bled into the terraces, with Senegal's Gaindé supporter group appearing to start jumping over the hoardings and onto the field in order to confront the officials and Moroccan delegation.

Stewards and riot police were forced to intervene, belatedly creating a barrier between the fans and the pitch, with projectiles being thrown onto the turf, and the Senegalese supporters jumping onto the electronic boardings and dismantling the display down one side of the pitch.

Several Senegal fans were removed by authorities, while one steward was taken out on a stretcher after appearing to sustain an injury to his upper body.

During the fracas, the Teranga Lions left the pitch upon instruction from head coach Pape Thiaw -- although it wasn't clear whether it was due to security reasons or in a protest at the referee's decision to belatedly award a penalty after [El Hadji Malick Diouf](http://espn.com/soccer/player/_/id/359796/el-hadji-malick-diouf) put his hands on Diaz in the box in the sixth minute of stoppage time.

Amidst further on-field scrapping between [Ismael Saibari](http://espn.com/soccer/player/_/id/304572/ismael-saibari) and [Abdoulaye Seck](http://espn.com/soccer/player/_/id/251614/abdoulaye-seck), and a booking for [Édouard Mendy](http://espn.com/soccer/player/_/id/238362/edouard-mendy) for appearing to scuff up the penalty spot, Diaz eventually stepped up to take the spotkick, but, overspilling with emotion, lacked all conviction and his disastrous Panenka attempt was easily claimed by the Teranga Lions goalkeeper.

It took the game to extra time, where Gueye's thunderous strike was enough for Senegal to win their second AFCON crown, with Morocco missing out on the chance to end their 50-year wait for a continental title with fairytale victory on home soil.

![Image 6: Pape Gueye scored soon for Senegal after the penalty, with Morocco not yet getting their heads back in the game.](https://a.espncdn.com/photo/2026/0118/r1602406_1296x729_16-9.jpg)

Pape Gueye scored soon for Senegal after the penalty, with Morocco not yet getting their heads back in the game.

SEBASTIEN BOZON / AFP via Getty Images

* * *

## One and a half hours earlier...

Morocco had Yacine Bounou to thank for the scores being level at the break, with the outstanding goalkeeper pulling off exceptional saves at either end of the first half to keep Senegal at bay.

In the fourth minute, Senegal ought to have gone ahead when Pape Gueye was picked out by [Lamine Camara](http://espn.com/soccer/player/_/id/38721/lamine-camara)'s cross at the backpost, with Bounou having initially misjudged the flight of the ball. However, the Morocco stopper readjusted in midair and swivelled his body in order to claw the midfielder's downward header around the post.

It was the clearest chance Morocco had faced from open play all tournament, as they received an early indication that Senegal would be a far sterner test than they've faced so far.

[Nigeria](http://espn.com/soccer/team?id=657) didn't earn a corner against the tournament hosts in Wednesday's semifinal until extra time, but here, Senegal managed it in the opening moments of the contest.

[Sadio Mané](http://espn.com/soccer/player/_/id/169797/sadio-mane) versus [Achraf Hakimi](http://espn.com/soccer/player/_/id/240233/achraf-hakimi) emerged as a key early battle, with Senegal complaining early that the referee was overlooking Morocco infractions with an early challenge on their skipper not being penalised, while [Iliman Ndiaye](http://espn.com/soccer/player/_/id/268641/iliman-ndiaye) was warned by the referee after bringing down [Noussair Mazraoui](http://espn.com/soccer/player/_/id/239350/noussair-mazraoui) despite appearing to get the ball.

[Abde Ezzalzouli](http://espn.com/soccer/player/_/id/300912/abde-ezzalzouli), so lively since his introduction to the starting XI earlier in the tournament, again proved to be Morocco's most effective outlet, getting an early cross in after outpacing rightback [Antoine Mendy](http://espn.com/soccer/player/_/id/319161/antoine-mendy), who had been forced to replace the outstanding [Krépin Diatta](http://espn.com/soccer/player/_/id/253992/krepin-diatta) at the last minute after the first-choice was taken sick during the warm-up.

Ismael Saibari had the next clear opportunity, bursting through as Senegal's defence appeared to open up for him before lashing wide on 13 minutes, before his blushes were spared by the offside flag soon afterwards.

[Ayoub El Kaabi](http://espn.com/soccer/player/_/id/269562/ayoub-el-kaabi) delayed in playing him in, and the [PSV Eindhoven](http://espn.com/soccer/team?id=148) attacker was clearly offside by the time he sent a poor effort into the side netting.

![Image 7: Morocco goalkeeper Yassine Bounou made an absolute blinder of a save in the 90th minute, the save of the tournament on balance.](https://a.espncdn.com/photo/2026/0118/r1602411_1296x729_16-9.jpg)

Morocco goalkeeper Yassine Bounou made an absolute blinder of a save in the 90th minute, the save of the tournament on balance.

FRANCK FIFE / AFP via Getty Images

* * *

Things became increasingly combative as the half progressed, with Camara booked for a sliding tackle on [Neil El Aynaoui](http://espn.com/soccer/player/_/id/323807/neil-el-aynaoui), with [Bilal El Khannouss](http://espn.com/soccer/player/_/id/336595/bilal-el-khannouss) arguably fortunate not to have received the same punishment after his zealous tackle on Pape Gueye.

On 38 minutes, Bounou made his second major intervention of the half, sticking out a foot to deny Ndiaye after the [Everton](http://espn.com/soccer/team?id=368) man was played in one on one beyond the outstretched Mazraoui by a delicious raking ball from [Nicolas Jackson](http://espn.com/soccer/player/_/id/308524/nicolas-jackson).

It was the first time Morocco had been truly prised apart by a team in open play during this tournament, with the palpable tension in the Prince Moulay Abdallah growing ever heavier as Senegal appeared increasingly unfazed by the relentless whistling from the majority home supporters whenever they touched the ball.

Morocco still enjoyed a threat of their own as the half came to a close, with [Nayef Aguerd](http://espn.com/soccer/player/_/id/245243/nayef-aguerd) only getting the faintest of headed touches on an Ezzalzouli cross after evading his marker, being unable to divert the chance towards goal.

The defender had to be on hand to squeeze out the advancing Mane, dancing down a left-hand channel, moments later, as each side sought to end the half in the ascendancy, with Moroccan last gasp-defending blocking a Camara shot from the edge of the box in first-half stoppage time.

While Senegal missed two gilt-edged opportunities to open the scoring in the first '45, it was Morocco who spurned the first major chance of the second half, as El Khannouss raced down the right flank before crossing superbly for El Kaabi, advancing quickly towards goal.

The striker, typically so instinctive in tight spots, took a moment to open up his body to finish, allowed sprawling Edouard Mendy in to close the angles, with El Kaabi's side-footed effort ultimately flying wide of the target.

Less than five minutes later, El Kaabi had another glorious chance. Being picked out by Diaz in the area, he thumped a left-footed effort towards goal, but [Mamadou Sarr](http://espn.com/soccer/player/_/id/355433/mamadou-sarr) -- in for the suspended [Kalidou Koulibaly](http://espn.com/soccer/player/_/id/150312/kalidou-koulibaly) -- was able to slide in and block the fierce attempt.

The game was halted in the 66th minute following a clash of heads that left El Aynaoui requiring extended treatment after he leapt to meet Hakimi's cross, only to connect with Diouf, who had similar intentions.

The midfielder received treatment for the best part of seven minutes, with blood continuing to leak from his head wound and requiring at least one change of shirt, but was eventually permitted to continue as play resumed.

![Image 8: Morocco's Neil El Aynaoui got medical attention for a few minutes late in the match, with a bang to the head wrapped up as it was bleeding.](https://a.espncdn.com/photo/2026/0118/r1602422_1296x729_16-9.jpg)

Morocco's Neil El Aynaoui got medical attention for a few minutes late in the match, with a bang to the head wrapped up as it was bleeding.

Torbjorn Tande/DeFodi Images/DeFodi via Getty Images

* * *

Morocco's momentum scarcely seemed impacted by the stoppage, and Ezzalzouli should have done better when found in space following a corner, with the wideman only able to send his shot down into the ground and into the arms of Mendy.

Approaching the final 10 minutes, each head coach turned to the bench, with Thiaw introducing [Ismaïla Sarr](http://espn.com/soccer/player/_/id/241012/ismaila-sarr) and wonderkid [Ibrahim Mbaye](http://espn.com/soccer/player/_/id/388522/ibrahim-mbaye), while Seck came on in the place of Antoine Mendy, while Walid Regragui added [Youssef En-Nesyri](http://espn.com/soccer/player/_/id/242736/youssef-en-nesyri) and Ouassama Targhalline for El Kaabi and El Khannouss.

An injury to [Adam Masina](http://espn.com/soccer/player/_/id/195988/adam-masina) in the 89th minute saw him leave the pitch in tears, with [Jawad El Yamiq](http://espn.com/soccer/player/_/id/232461/jawad-el-yamiq) entering to partner Aguerd as he had done following [Romain Saïss](http://espn.com/soccer/player/_/id/167686/romain-saiss)'s injury in the tournament opener against [Comoros](http://espn.com/soccer/team?id=8601).

With Morocco still regrouping after that setback, Bounou made his third big save of the contest, leaping to his right to paw away a curling effort from Mbaye, cutting inside and curling an effort towards goal, with Ezzalzouli then going straight up the other end and firing over on the swivel, under pressure from Seck.

Then to stoppage time, where refereeing decisions in both boxes left Senegalese fans incensed.

Senegal hadn't previously scored in three finals (2002, 2019, 2021), but thought they'd nabbed a winner in the third minute of eight minutes of stoppage time, when Seck's header rattled off the woodwork from a corner after beating Bounou, before Ismaila Sarr stopped to head home.

The referee immediately blew after determining that Seck had pushed Hakimi before taking his header, although the African Footballer of the Year appeared to go to ground remarkably easily.

This incensed Thiaw and the small group of Senegal fans in attendance, who were then further enraged when, after extended protests from Diaz, both to the linesman and the referee, Morocco were awarded a penalty in the 96th minute when Diouf's arms on Diaz appeared to impede him as a corner came in.

![Image 9: ...and popped it gently into Edouard Mendy's waiting arms.](https://a.espncdn.com/photo/2026/0118/r1602400_1296x729_16-9.jpg)

...and popped it gently into Edouard Mendy's waiting arms.

Paul ELLIS / AFP via Getty Images

* * *

Again, it appeared to be a soft decision going the way of the hosts, and this proved too much for Thiaw, his technical staff, and eventually, the Senegalese supporters, to take, prompting the clashes that took over 10 minutes to resolve.

Diaz's missed penalty stunned the over-66,000 in attendance in Rabat, or at least those who hand't been escorted out by police, with only a brief moment of pause before the contest resumed for extra time.

Morocco, appearing utterly windswept and disoriented after Diaz's fluffed penalty, were in disarray as Senegal finally opened the scoring for real, with Gueye meeting Idrissa Gana Gueye's layoff to slam a thunderous effort beyond Bounou with his left to turn the tide back in the Teranga Lions' favour.

Thereafter, the contest was frenetic and fierce, with both En-Nesyri and fellow substitute Hamza Igamane appearing to target Mendy, perhaps in response to his antics during the extended pause, but the goalkeeper holding his nerve to deny Diaz, while En-Nesyri missed a glorious chance from six yards after he could only meet Ezzalzouli's cross with a wayward header.

An Aguerd header then hit the crossbar with a header early in the second period of extra time as Morocco threw caution to the wind in search of an equaliser, before Mendy was called into action again as Senegal hung on by a thread.

They still offered menace down the other end though, as Morocco became increasingly disjointed, with Bounou forced into a low save to deny substitute [Cherif Ndiaye](http://espn.com/soccer/player/_/id/251924/cherif-ndiaye), who couldn't believe he'd failed to kill the target as the keeper stuck out a fingertip to prevent the striker from following up.

Gueye also fired another thumping effort straight at Bounou as things increasingly broke down, while the fight slowly ebbed away from Morocco as the clock ticked down.

On the final whistle, Senegal ran over to celebrate with their besieged supporters, still barracked by multiplied rows of riot police and stadium officials, while Morocco's players, shattered, collapsed to the ground apparently in a collective state of shock.

The Nigerian national cricket team‘s quest to win the ICC World T20 Africa Qualifier ‘A’ continued yesterday when the side recorded a convincing 55 runs victory over The Gambian at the Tafawa Balewa Cricket Oval in Lagos.
Captain Chimezie Onwuzulike’s decision to bat first after winning the toss paid off as Nigeria posted 176 runs for loss of five wickets in 20 overs. Basiru Jaye was the best bowler for the fielding side with two wickets, 16 runs in three overs.

Vice Captain, Ademola Onikoyi, top scored with 74 runs not out off 39 balls with nine fours and two sixes. Chimezie Onwuzulike added 34 runs, Isaac Okpe put in 21 runs not out with lovely three sixes and Opening batsman, Sulaimon Runsewe dropped 18 runs.  
  
 The Nigerian bowlers in the second innings ensured the mountain was too high for Captain Mbye Dumbuya’s team to climb as The Gambia was reduced to 121 runs for seven wickets in 20 overs.

Debutant Daniel Gim claimed two wickets for 16 runs in three overs, while the quartet of Isaac Danladi, Shola Anyia, Seye Olympio and Isaac Okpe all had a wicket each.

Advertisement

Pa Assan Faye led the batting onslaught for his side with 29 runs off 16 balls, Mohammed Manga 24 runs and Andrew Jarju contributed 15 runs.

This victory (Nigeria has won two matches, including the opening victory against Sierra Leone and the defeat of The Gambia) means that qualification for the next stage of the qualifiers is in sight.

The big decider of which team will top the qualifier will come on Tuesday when Nigeria clashes with bitter rivals, Ghana at the same venue.

Player of the Match is **Tom Banton**: "As a kid you dream of scoring a hundred for your country. To do it here in an important game was really special, had lots of friends and family here as well. Player of the Series is **Will Jacks**: [Back so soon after appendix out] "Was hoping so, as soon as I had surgery. Always very grateful to play for your country and for the series I've had. Sri Lanka captain **Kusal Mendis**: "We played a couple of good games, but today we struggled batting. We dropped some catching, bad fielding [cost us]. Building towards a squad where if someone does go down, someone else can come in and perform. With Daws coming in and picking up three wickets, you can see we're building towards that. [Next few weeks] Go away, train and get ready for a fairly long winter."

## About this app

_arrow\_forward_

Moneycontrol App is Asia's #1 App for Business & Finance - Track markets, get loans, do financial transactions, and more.  
  
Track the latest updates on Indian and Global financial markets on your smartphone with the Moneycontrol App. It covers multiple assets from BSE, NSE, MCX and NCDEX exchanges to track Indices (Sensex & Nifty), Stocks, Futures, Options, Mutual Funds, Commodities. Additionally, the app facilitates personal loans and fixed deposits.  
  
Monitor your investments with Portfolio and Watchlist. Stay updated with the full range of news covered in our News and Personal Finance sections. Get expert views & in-depth coverage of the financial markets with live streaming of CNBC  
  
Moneycontrol App Offers:  
⦿ Seamless Navigation:  
Effortlessly browse your portfolio, markets data, latest news, watchlist, forum, and more.  
⦿ Latest Market Data:  
Get real-time quotes for stocks, F&O, mutual funds, commodities from BSE, NSE, MCX, and NCDEX.  
Stay updated with prices for Sensex, NIFTY, India VIX, and more.  
Access in-depth market stats for stocks, futures, and options.  
Explore interactive charts: Line, Area, Candlestick, and OHLC.  
⦿ News:  
Stay informed with the latest market, business, and economy news.  
Enjoy exclusive interviews with top business leaders.  
Use the ‘Text to Speech’ feature to listen to news and articles on the go.  
⦿ Portfolio:  
Easily monitor your portfolio across stocks, mutual funds, and other assets.  
⦿ Personalized Watchlist:  
Track your favourite stocks, mutual funds, commodities, futures effortlessly.  
⦿ Forum:  
Engage with your favorite topics and follow top boarders for insights.  
  
Moneycontrol Pro Offers:  
‣ Ad-free Experience  
‣ Personalized News for your portfolio  
‣ Insights, Analysis, and Trends with sharp commentary to help make better investment decisions  
‣ Ideas for Profit from our in-house and independent research team  
‣ Technical Analysis by professional chartists  
‣ Smart Calendar of business and economic events  
‣ Guru Speak - lessons from successful investors  
  
Moneycontrol Pro subscriptions:   
• Monthly - INR 99 per Month (India) or $1.40 (outside India)  
• Quarterly - INR 289 for 3 Months (India) or $4.09 (outside India)  
• Annual - INR 999 for 1 year (India) or $14.13 (outside India)  
  
Personal Loan: (available in India only)  
Moneycontrol provides a curated platform to get instant personal loan from India’s top lenders.  
Lenders on Moneycontrol Platform   
- NBFCs: Bhanix Finance & Investment Ltd (Cashe), L&T Finance Limited (L&T), Earlysalary Services Private Limited (Fibe)  
- Aggregator: QFI Technologies Private Limited (Niro)  
  
Need to know more about loan structure? we have covered with below important pointers:  
• Loan Tenure : 6 to 60 months  
• Max Annual Percentage Rate (APR) : 36%  
• Sample loan breakdown :  
Loan Amount : Rs 1,00,000/-, Tenure: 3 years, Rate of Interest : 15 %  
Principal : 1,00,000  
Interest on the loan : 24,795  
Monthly Payment for 36 months : 3,467  
Processing fees : Approx. 2,000  
Please note : Moneycontrol is not directly engaged in money lending activities. We only provide a platform to facilitate money lending by registered Non-Banking Financial Companies (NBFCs) or banks to users.  
  
Note:  
Your Moneycontrol Pro subscription will renew automatically through your Google Play account. You can cancel auto-renewal at any time from the subscription list in your Google Play account. There will be No Refund or Credit for partial monthly subscription periods.  
  
We are excited to announce that Moneycontrol is offering Fixed Deposits.  
To book a FD, users need to complete a one-time SIM binding.  
To Create FD user must follow steps   
• Tap on Fixed Deposits  
• Provide Permission for Sim Binding Process  
• Select your preferred FD   
• Complete KYC  
• Complete your FD payments via UPI or Net banking.
